props.description: A therapeutic modality that delivers a physical agent (e.g. heat, cold, light, electricity) to the body for therapeutic purposes.

props.name: biofeedback
props.description: Assisting the patient to modify a body function using feedback from instrumentation.

props.name: cryotherapy
props.description: A form of therapy consisting of the local or general use of cold.

props.name: cryocuff treatment
props.description: Cryocuff treatment uses a device that circulates ice cold water to provide cold therapy in the treatment of injuries.

props.name: ice pack application
props.description: Application of an ice pack to an injured area. A thin fabric should be placed on the skin to buffer the skin from the ice.

props.name: thermotherapy
props.description: The application of heat to appropriate painful areas to improve blood flow and function and to reduce pain. It can be applied though many methods, using convection, conduction, or radiation. Conduction uses hydrocollator, paraffin, or other similar methods. Convection uses immersion hydrotherapy, immersion, forced fluidotherapy, and radiant heat. Radiation uses laser.

props.name: thermotherapy with hot packs
props.description: Applying heat to a client's body part or region for therapeutic effect(s) (for example, to increase circulation).

props.name: shortwave diathermy
props.description: The therapeutic elevation of temperature in the tissues by means of an oscillating electric current of extremely high frequency.

props.name: low-level laser therapy
props.description: Treatment using irradiation with LASER light of low power intensity so that the effects are not due to heat, as they are in LASER THERAPY.

props.name: pulsed electromagnetic energy therapy
props.description: Therapy using pulsed electromagnetic energy.

props.name: electrotherapy
props.description: Application of electric current in treatment without the generation of perceptible heat. It includes electric stimulation of nerves or muscles, passage of current into the body, or use of interrupted current of low intensity to raise the threshold of the skin to pain.

props.name: phototherapy
props.description: The treatment of disease with certain types of light. Phototherapy can use lasers, LED, fluorescent lamps, and ultraviolet or infrared radiation.

props.name: neuromuscular electrical stimulation
props.description: A procedure in which small electric impulses are used to stimulate muscles that are weak or paralyzed. It helps to increase muscle strength, blood circulation, and range of motion and to lessen muscle spasms.

props.name: transcutaneous electric nerve stimulation
props.description: Stimulation of skin and underlying tissues with controlled, low-voltage electrical vibration via electrodes.

props.name: interferential therapy
props.description: Interferential therapy (IFT) is a type of physical therapy. It uses a mid-frequency electrical signal to treat muscular spasms and strains.

props.name: exercise
props.description: Physical activity as practiced in recreation, amateur and professional sports, or planned activity to improve physical condition or health.

props.name: functional exercise
props.description: Functional training is a classification of exercise which involves training the body for the activities performed in daily life.

props.name: walking
props.description: An activity in which the body advances at a slow to moderate pace by moving the feet in a coordinated fashion. This includes recreational walking, walking for fitness, and competitive race-walking.

props.name: Nordic walking
props.description: Nordic walking is a physical activity and a sport. The activity is performed with specially designed walking poles similar to ski poles.

props.name: hiking
props.description: Hiking is an outdoor activity which consists of walking in natural environments, often in mountainous or other scenic terrain.

props.name: power walking
props.description: Power walking or speed walking is the act of walking with a speed at the upper end of the natural range for walking gait, typically 7 to 9 km/h (4.5 to 5.5 mph). To qualify as power walking as opposed to jogging or running, at least one foot must be in contact with the ground at all times.

props.name: jogging
props.description: Running at a low rate of speed. It can be done as a means of conditioning or for general health and well being.

props.name: running
props.description: An activity in which the body is propelled by moving the legs rapidly. Running is performed at a moderate to rapid pace and should be differentiated from JOGGING, which is performed at a much slower pace.

props.name: water running
props.description: A non-impact form of running performed in a swimming pool.

props.name: squats
props.description: Start position: Stand upright with feet shoulder width apart. Action: Slowly bend knees until the thighs are parallel to the floor, then slowly straighten knees back to the start position. Variations: sliding up and down the wall; adding hand weights; varying the trunk angle; varying the feet positioning; adding calf raises when rising from the squat; on an uneven or unstable surface; throwing a ball at a target; adding upper body movements.

props.name: basic squats
props.description: Start position: Stand upright with feet shoulder width apart. Action: Slowly bend knees until the thighs are parallel to the floor, then slowly straighten knees back to the start position.

props.name: lunges
props.description: A lunge can refer to any position of the human body where one leg is positioned forward with knee bent and foot flat on the ground while the other leg is positioned behind.

props.name: step ups
props.description: Start position: Place the affected leg on the step. Action: Rise up onto the step by slowly straightening the affected knee while maintaining the balance on that leg. Keep the affected leg on the step and slowly bend the affected knee until the other foot lightly touches the floor. Variations: adding hand weights.

props.name: swimming
props.description: The act of propelling the body through water by movement of the arms and/or legs.

props.name: balance exercise
props.description: Use of specific activities, postures, and movements to maintain, enhance, or restore balance.

props.name: plyometric exercise
props.description: Exercises in which muscles are repeatedly and rapidly stretched, followed by shortening, concentric MUSCLE CONTRACTION (e.g. jumping and rebounding). They are designed to exert maximal force in minimal time by increasing STRETCH REFLEX.

props.name: hopping
props.description: A light springy jump or leap, especially on one foot.

props.name: jumping
props.description: Moving up off the ground by bending and extending the legs, such as jumping on one foot, hopping, skipping and jumping or diving into water.

props.name: skipping
props.description: A cardiopulmonary exercise in which one jumps over a swinging rope.

props.name: trampolining
props.description: Bouncing on a trampoline.

props.name: range of motion exercise
props.description: Actions performed to provide the active or passive exercises to maintain joint function.

props.name: muscle strength exercise
props.description: An exercise that incorporates muscular contractions to improve muscular strength.

props.name: resistance exercise
props.description: A type of strength-building exercise program that requires the body muscle to exert a force against some form of resistance, such as weight, stretch bands, water, or immovable objects. Resistance exercise is a combination of static and dynamic contractions involving shortening and lengthening of skeletal muscles.

props.name: flexibility exercise
props.description: An exercise designed to improve flexibility or range of motion.

props.name: stretching exercise
props.description: Facilitation of systematic slow-stretch-hold muscle exercises to induce relaxation, to prepare muscles/joints for more vigorous exercise, or to increase or maintain body flexibility.

props.name: aerobic exercise
props.description: Physical activity that increases the heart rate and the body's use of oxygen. It helps improve a person's physical fitness.

props.name: cycling
props.description: Cycling is the use of bicycles for transport, recreation, or for sport.

props.name: rowing
props.description: An exercise performed on a rowing machine.

props.name: stepper machine exercise
props.description: An exercise performed on a stepper.

props.name: elliptical motion exercise
props.description: An exercise performed on an elliptical motion exercise.

props.name: mobility device
props.description: Mobility aids help you walk or move from place to place if you are disabled or have an injury. They include crutches, canes, walkers, wheelchairs and motorized scooters.

props.name: orthopedic braces
props.description: An orthopedic device used to support a moveable body part.

props.name: biomedical tape
props.description: A long thin piece of cloth or paper as used for binding or fastening.

props.name: orthotic device
props.description: A device applied to a human limb to control or enhance movement or to prevent bone movement or deformity, for example, a splint or an arch support.

props.name: exerciser
props.description: A device for exercising the body.

props.name: aerobic exerciser
props.description: Exerciser designed to facilitate the physical exertion of body muscles by the voluntary contraction and relaxation of large muscle groups (i.e., active exercisers), which are intended primarily for making users breathe more deeply and their hearts work harder; activities in aerobic exercises can be usually maintained continuously and are rhythmic in nature. Dedicated aerobic exercisers are available for walking and jogging (e.g., treadmills), cycling (e.g., stationary bicycles), and other activities such as rowing, elliptical motion, or bouncing.

props.name: elliptical motion exerciser
props.description: Aerobic exercisers designed to simulate elliptical (in an oval plane) motions, a combination of stair-stepping, running, cross-country skiing, and walking.

props.name: stationary bicycle
props.description: Aerobic cycle exercisers designed to simulate the motions of riding a bicycle; the bicycles remain stationary while the wheels move.

props.name: bicycle
props.description: A bicycle is a human-powered, pedal-driven, single-track vehicle, having two wheels attached to a frame, one behind the other.

props.name: rowing machine
props.description: Aerobic exercisers designed to simulate the motions of rowing (i.e., propelling a boat forward using oars).

props.name: stepper
props.description: Climbing aerobic exercisers designed to simulate the motion of climbing stairs using movable stairs or steppers.

props.name: treadmill
props.description: Aerobic exercisers designed to allow the user to exercise by walking and/or running on a moving belt.

props.name: balance exerciser
props.description: Exercisers designed for the physical exertion of body muscles by voluntary contraction and relaxation of the muscles, which are intended primarily to improve the user's ability to maintain proper posture and stability. Dedicated balance exercisers are available in the forms of balls, discs, boards, domes, and rollers.

props.name: wobble cushion
props.description: A small inflatable cushion, strong enough to sit or stand on, used to create instability.

props.name: balance mat
props.description: A pad made of unstable material used to create instability while exercising.

props.name: pro-fitter physio kit
props.description: A multifunctional balance and fitness tool.

props.name: wobble board
props.description: Board balance exerciser that consists of a round, flat, wooden or plastic board with a plastic, semispherical fulcrum attached underneath; they can usually be moved in multiple angular degrees, and tile angles are also adjustable.

props.name: rocker board
props.description: Board balance exerciser that consists of a flat, square or rectangular, wooden board and a wooden or plastic fulcrum attached underneath.

props.name: balance ball
props.description: Balance exerciser that consists of a synthetic or rubber ball approximately 65 cm in diamter.

props.name: muscle strength exerciser
props.description: Exercisers designed primarily to facilitate the physical exertion of body muscles by voluntary contraction and relaxation of large muscle groups (i.e., active exercisers) that are intended primarily to provide resistance to muscular contraction for development of muscular strength and endurance. The resistance to muscular contractions may be provided by gravity using free weights or constrained weights, hydraulic resistance mechanisms, elastic resistance, or other sources.

props.name: elastic resistance exerciser
props.description: Strength exercisers designed to provide elastic resistance to muscular contraction for developing muscular strength and endurance. These exercisers typically consist of an elastic material such as a flexible (e.g., rubber) band or tube or a coiled metal spring; the elastic resistance increases as the elastic element is stretched.

props.name: free weight
props.description: Muscle strength exercisers designed to provide resistance to muscular contraction using unconstrained weighted plates; the resistance is provided by the force of gravity acting on the free weights. Free weights are not attached to any other devices and do not restrict the user's movements; they usually include barbells and dumbbells.

props.name: dumbbell
props.description: Free weight exercisers designed to provide resistance to muscular contraction using two weight plates connected by a short bar (i.e., dumbbells and weight); the resistance is provided by the force of gravity acting on the dumbbells.

props.name: kettlebell
props.description: The kettlebell is a cast-iron weight (resembling a cannonball with a handle) used to perform ballistic exercises that combine cardiovascular, strength and flexibility training.

props.name: barbell
props.description: Free weight exercisers designed to provide resistance to muscular contraction. These devices are long bars with removable weighted disks attached to each end. Using the weight on the barbells, resistance is provided by the force of gravity acting on the barbell.

props.name: weight machine
props.description: Muscle strength exercisers designed to provide resistance to muscular contraction using a mechanism based on a system of pulleys and cables or levers; resistance may be provided by the force of gravity exerted on constrained weight stacks, by a hydraulic mechanism in which resistance changes in proportion to the force exerted on it, or by any other appropriate means. These exercisers usually consist of a stand-alone machine with weights stacked on top of each other and/or a hydraulic piston, a system to transmit the force (i.e., to convey the resistance), and lever bars or pulley cables on which the user exerts force to counteract the exerciser resistance. Dedicated lever-pulley-cable exercisers intended to improve the strength in full body or specific body muscle groups such as the upper and lower limbs, trunk, and neck are available; the exercisers may also increase muscle size, muscle endurance, and power and improve bone density.

props.name: knee extension resistance machine
props.description: Muscle strength exercisers designed to provide resistance to muscular contraction when the legs are extended against the resistance using a mechanism based on a system of pulleys and cables or levers. These exercisers usually consist of a stand-alone machine with weights stacked on top of each other or a hydraulic mechanism, a system to transmit the force (i.e., to convey the resistance), and lever bars or cables on which the user exerts force to counteract the exerciser resistance. Typically, users lift a padded lever bar with their ankles to extend the knees; less frequently, using the legs, the users pull the cables to extend their knees.

props.name: knee flexion resistance machine
props.description: Muscle strength exercisers designed to provide resistance to muscular contraction when the knees are flexed against resistance using equipment based on a system of pulleys and cables or levers. These exercisers usually consist of a stand-alone machine with weights stacked on top of each other or a hydraulic mechanism, a system to transmit the force (i.e., to convey the resistance), and lever bars or pulley cables on which the user exerts force to counteract the exerciser resistance. Lever bar machines require the users to push a padded lever bar down with their ankles to flex their knees toward the back of their thighs or lie prone and, with the pads above the ankles, flex the knees toward the back of their thighs; using pulley-cable machines, the users attach the cable to their ankles and flex the knees.

props.name: hip abduction resistance machine
props.description: Lower-limb muscle strength exercisers based on a system of levers that are designed to provide resistance to muscular contraction when the user performs hip abduction. The user exerts force on levers to counteract the exerciser resistance. These exercisers are usually stand-alone machines consisting of weights stacked on top of each other, a system to transmit the force (i.e., to convey the resistance), and a seat with two padded levers attached, one on each side, and foot rests at the bottom. Typically, the user sits in the seat with the sides of their knees and legs resting on the padded levers and their feet on the foot rests. The user puts one thigh inside each padded lever and pushes outwards against the resistance.

props.name: hip adduction resistance machine
props.description: Lower-limb muscle strength exercisers based on a system of levers that are designed to provide resistance to muscular contraction when the user performs hip adduction. The user exerts force on levers to counteract the exerciser resistance. These exercisers are usually stand-alone machines consisting of weights stacked on top of each other, a system to transmit the force (i.e., to convey the resistance), and a seat with two padded levers attached, one on each side, and foot rests at the bottom. Typically, the user sits in the seat with the sides of their knees and legs resting on the padded levers and their feet on the foot rests. The user puts one thigh outside each padded lever and pushes inwards.

props.name: leg press machine
props.description: Muscle strength exercisers designed to provide resistance to muscular contraction when the feet press against resistance using a mechanism based on a system of levers. These exercisers usually consist of a stand-alone machine with weights stacked on top of each other or a hydraulic mechanism, a system to transmit the force (i.e., to convey the resistance), and lever bars on which the user exerts force to counteract the exerciser resistance. Users place their feet on a platform and push it away to extend the knees. Leg press exercisers are intended to improve the strength in the leg muscles (e.g., quadriceps, gluteus, hamstring, calves), increase muscle size, enhance muscle endurance and power, and improve bone density.

props.name: fitness accessory
props.description: An exerciser that is not a machine.

props.name: medicine ball
props.description: A medicine ball is a weighted ball roughly the diameter of the shoulders.

props.name: skipping rope
props.description: Aerobic exercisers that may consist simply of a rope or cord that users swing over themselves and jump or skip over each time it reaches the feet and the two handles that users hold. The cords may be made of nylon, polyvinyl, cotton, steel, leather, or rubber, and some cords may be braided or segmented and/or permit length adjustment; the handles can be wooden or plastic and may be mounted with removable weights to add resistance to the muscles involved in the exercise.

props.name: trampoline
props.description: A trampoline is a device consisting of a piece of taut, strong fabric stretched over a steel frame using many coiled springs.

props.name: football
props.description: A football is an inflated ball used to play one of the various sports known as football.

props.name: step
props.description: A support consisting of a place to rest the foot while ascending or descending a stairway.

props.name: skateboard
props.description: A short narrow board having a set of four wheels mounted under it.

props.name: trekking pole
props.description: A common hiking accessory used to assist walkers with their rhythm and provide stability on rough terrain.

props.name: pain
props.description: The sensation of discomfort, distress, or agony, resulting from the stimulation of specialized nerve endings.

props.name: swelling
props.description: Enlargement; expansion in size; sign of inflammation.

props.name: giving-way
props.description: The sensation of a joint (e.g. knee or hip) failing to properly support the weight of the body.

props.name: joint instability
props.description: Lack of stability of a joint or joint prosthesis. Factors involved are intra-articular disease and integrity of extra-articular structures such as joint capsule, ligaments, and muscles.

props.name: joint stiffness
props.description: A sensation of discomfort and tightness while moving a joint. Typically there is decreased joint range of motion. Causes include arthritis, joint overuse, joint injury, and the aging process.

props.name: symptom management
props.description: Care alleviating symptoms without curing the underlying disease (Stedman, 25th ed).

props.name: RICE
props.description: RICE is a first-aid treatment method for soft tissue injuries which is an acronym for Rest, Ice, Compression and Elevation.

props.name: weight management
props.description: Deliberate regulation of one's weight through diet, exercise, or other means. Also, the relative weight change resulting from such regulation practices.

props.name: pathological condition
props.description: Pathological structure, disposition, or process. This disjoint category helps properly represent diseases because it is often left open whether they are meant as pathological structure, disposition, or process.

props.name: disease
props.description: A disposition (i) to undergo pathological processes that (ii) exists in an organism because of one or more disorders in that organism.

props.name: injury
props.description: A part of an organism that has undergone a change in structural integrity and has a higher chance of dysfunction or causing dysfunction in another structure.

props.name: dislocation
props.description: Dislocations are joint injuries that force the ends of your bones out of position. When a dislocation occurs, you cannot move the joint. You can dislocate your ankles, knees, shoulders, hips and elbows. Dislocated joints often are swollen, very painful and visibly out of place.

props.name: fracture
props.description: Breaks or rupture in bones or cartilages.

props.name: open fracture
props.description: Fractures in which there is an external wound communicating with the break of the bone.

props.name: closed fracture
props.description: A fracture in which the break in bone is not accompanied by an external wound.

props.name: tear
props.description: Forcible tearing or disruption of tissue.

props.name: bucket-handle tear
props.description: A bucket-handle tear of a meniscus is a longitudinal tear with an attached fragment displaced away from the meniscus.

props.name: parrot-beak tear
props.description: A type of radial tear which begins at the inner edge, but then curves into a longitudinal orientation as the tear extends toward the meniscal periphery.

props.name: flap tear
props.description: A tear with a flap displaced to the vertical or horizontal direction.

props.name: surface tear
props.description: A tear that reaches the surface of an organ such as meniscus.

props.name: intrasubstance tear
props.description: A tear that occurs within the substance of an organ and does not reach its surface.

props.name: radial tear
props.description: A short tear that extends from the inner edge of the meniscus towards the outer part of the meniscus.

props.name: vertical tear
props.description: A tear in the meniscus with a vertical direction.

props.name: peripheral tear
props.description: A tear that occurs in the periphery of an organ.

props.name: longitudinal tear
props.description: A tear in the meniscus with a longitudinal direction.

props.name: horizontal cleavage tear
props.description: A tear in the meniscus with a horizontal direction.

props.name: degenerative tear
props.description: A tear that occurs due to wear and tear (degeneration) of the meniscal cartilage.

props.name: undisplaced tear
props.description: A tear with a torn fragment still in place.

props.name: displaced tear
props.description: A tear with a displaced fragment of an organ.

props.name: partial tear
props.description: A tear that does not completely disrupt the tissue.

props.name: complete tear
props.description: A tear that splits the tissue into two pieces.

props.name: bone contusion
props.description: A compression injury of the bone, which is usually associated with a bone bruise.

props.name: subluxation
props.description: An incomplete dislocation of a joint.

props.name: extrusion
props.description: A thrusting or forcing out of a normal position.

props.name: sprains or strain
props.description: A sprain is a stretched or torn ligament. A strain is a stretched or torn muscle or tendon.

props.name: sprain
props.description: A sprain is a stretched or torn ligament.

props.name: strain
props.description: A strain is a stretched or torn muscle or tendon.

props.name: arthritis
props.description: An inflammatory process affecting a joint. Causes include infection, autoimmune processes, degenerative processes, and trauma. Signs and symptoms may include swelling around the affected joint and pain.

props.name: osteophyte
props.description: Bony outgrowth usually found around joints and often seen in conditions such as ARTHRITIS.

props.name: osteoarthritis
props.description: A noninflammatory degenerative joint disease occurring chiefly in older persons, characterised by degeneration of the articular cartilage, hypertrophy of bone at the margins and changes in the synovial membrane. It is accompanied by pain and stiffness, particularly after prolonged activity.

props.name: rheumatoid arthritis
props.description: Chronic systemic disease, primarily of the joints, marked by inflammatory changes in the synovial membranes and articular structures, widespread fibrinoid degeneration of the collagen fibers in mesenchymal tissues, and by atrophy and rarefaction of bony structures; etiology is unknown, but autoimmune mechanisms have been implicated.

props.name: popliteal cyst
props.description: A benign swelling found behind the knee joint.

props.name: chondromalacia patellae
props.description: A degeneration of the ARTICULAR CARTILAGE of the PATELLA, caused by a decrease in sulfated MUCOPOLYSACCHARIDES in the ground substance. When accompanied by pain, it is sometimes considered part of or confused with PATELLOFEMORAL PAIN SYNDROME.

props.name: discoid meniscus
props.description: A discoid meniscus is an abnormally shaped meniscus in the knee.It is shaped like a half moon or complete circle, rather than a crescent moon.

props.name: bursitis
props.description: Inflammation or irritation of a bursa, the fibrous sac that acts as a cushion between moving structures of bones, muscles, tendons or skin.

props.name: synovitis
props.description: Inflammation of a synovial membrane.

props.name: osteochondritis dissecans
props.description: A type of osteochondritis in which articular cartilage and associated bone becomes partially or totally detached to form joint loose bodies. Affects mainly the knee, ankle, and elbow joints.

props.name: osteonecrosis
props.description: Death of bone tissue due to traumatic or nontraumatic causes.

props.name: tendinopathy
props.description: Clinical syndrome describing overuse tendon injuries characterized by a combination of PAIN, diffuse or localized swelling, and impaired performance. Distinguishing tendinosis from tendinitis is clinically difficult and can be made only after histopathological examination.

props.name: tendinitis
props.description: Inflammation of TENDONS. It is characterized by the degeneration of tendons accompanied by an inflammatory repair response, fibroblastic proliferation, and formation of granulation tissue. Tendinitis is not a clinical diagnosis and can be confirmed only by histopathological findings.

props.name: tendinosis
props.description: A disorder of TENDONS characterized by COLLAGEN degeneration, other changes to tenocytes and the EXTRACELLULAR MATRIX, and a lack of inflammatory cells. It is caused by aging, microtrauma, or vascular compromise. Tendinosis is not a clinical diagnosis and can be confirmed only by histopathological findings.

props.name: patellofemoral pain syndrome
props.description: A syndrome characterized by retropatellar or peripatellar PAIN resulting from physical and biochemical changes in the patellofemoral joint. The pain is most prominent when ascending or descending stairs, squatting, or sitting with flexed knees.

props.name: iliotibial band syndrome
props.description: An overuse injury causing lateral knee pain that results from repetitive friction of the iliotibial band over the lateral femoral epicondyle.

props.name: impingement
props.description: Joint impingement is a painful syndrome caused by the friction of joint tissues, which is both the cause and the effect of altered joint biomechanics. From the anatomical and clinical viewpoints, these syndromes are classified as bone impingement, soft tissue impingement and entrapment neuropathy, depending on what joint portion impinges on the others.

props.name: internal derangement of knee
props.description: A non specific term used to cover a group of disorders involving disruption of the normal functioning of the knee joint.

props.name: surgery
props.description: A diagnostic or treatment procedure performed by manual and/or instrumental means, often involving an incision and the removal or replacement of a diseased organ or tissue; of or relating to or involving or used in surgery or requiring or amenable to treatment by surgery.

props.name: reconstructive surgery
props.description: Procedures used to reconstruct, restore, or improve defective, damaged, or missing structures.

props.name: arthroscopy
props.description: Endoscopic examination, therapy and surgery of the joint.

props.name: surgical repair
props.description: Restoring, to the extent possible, the natural anatomical structure.

props.name: osteotomy
props.description: Surgical cutting or removal of bone.

props.name: autologous chondrocyte implantation
props.description: A biomedical treatment that repairs damages in articular cartilage.

props.name: arthroplasty
props.description: Surgical reconstruction or replacement of all or part of a malformed, diseased, degenerated, or otherwise damaged joint.

props.name: joint replacement
props.description: Partial or total replacement of a joint.

props.name: fracture fixation
props.description: The use of metallic devices inserted into or through bone to hold a fracture in a set position and alignment while it heals.

props.name: crutches
props.description: A wooden or metal staff that fits under the armpit and reaches to the ground, used as an aid while walking.

props.name: cane
props.description: A cane is a device intended for medical purposes that is used to provide minimal weight support while walking. Examples of canes include the following: A standard cane, a forearm cane, and a cane with a tripod, quad, or retractable stud on the ground end.

props.name: organismal quality
props.description: A quality that inheres in an entire organism or part of an organism.

props.name: behavioral quality
props.description: An organismal quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's behavior aggregate of the responses or reactions or movements in a given situation.

props.name: movement behavioral quality
props.description: A behavioral quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's movement.

props.name: active
props.description: A behavioral quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's exhibiting movement as a result of its own action.

props.name: passive
props.description: A behavioral quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's exhibiting movement as a result of an externally applied force.

props.name: balance
props.description: A behavioral quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of having physical steadiness.

props.name: coordination
props.description: A behavioral quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's having or lacking skillful and effective interaction of movement.

props.name: range of motion
props.description: The distance and direction to which a bone joint can be extended. Range of motion is a function of the condition of the joints, muscles, and connective tissues involved. Joint flexibility can be improved through appropriate MUSCLE STRETCHING EXERCISES.

props.name: muscle tone
props.description: Condition of moderate contraction produced by stretching a muscle.

props.name: muscle strength
props.description: Force exerted by a muscle, as a response parameter (e.g. bioassay) or as an indicator of health, endurance, fitness, etc.

props.name: muscle endurance
props.description: The ability of a muscle to sustain repeated contractions against a resistance for an extended period of time.

props.name: physical endurance
props.description: The time span between the beginning of physical activity by an individual and the termination because of exhaustion.

props.name: physical fitness
props.description: The ability to carry out daily tasks and perform physical activities in a highly functional state, often as a result of physical conditioning.

props.name: physical strength
props.description: Degree of intensity or force in regard to a physical activity.

props.name: physical agility
props.description: The ability to change the body's position efficiently.

props.name: joint stability
props.description: The resistance offered by various musculoskeletal tissues that surround a skeletal joint.

props.name: body power
props.description: Functions related to the force generated by the contraction of all muscles and muscle groups of the body.

props.name: muscle power
props.description: The ability of a msucle to generate as much force as fast as possible.

props.name: postoperative complication
props.description: Pathologic processes that affect patients after a surgical procedure. They may or may not be related to the disease for which the surgery was done, and they may or may not be direct results of the surgery.

props.name: hematoma
props.description: A localized collection of blood, usually clotted, in an organ, space, or tissue, due to a break in the wall of a blood vessel.

props.name: phlebitis
props.description: Inflammation of a vein, often a vein in the leg.

props.name: reflex sympathetic dystrophy
props.description: A rare neurologic syndrome characterized by burning pain, tenderness, swelling, and changes in the skin color and temperature of a body part or extremity. It is usually caused by injury or surgery.

props.name: infection
props.description: Invasion and growth of microorganisms in body tissues.

props.name: deep vein thrombosis
props.description: A blood clot (thrombus) in a deep vein in the thigh or leg.

props.name: outpatient care
props.description: Health care services provided to patients on an ambulatory basis, rather than by admission to a hospital or other health care facility. The services may be a part of a hospital, augmenting its inpatient services, or may be provided at a free-standing facility.

props.name: motivating patient
props.description: Improvements in patient motivation could be brought about by the therapist adopting specific qualities and modes of behaviour towards patients. These are: a constantly positive and encouraging attitude towards the patient; a willingness to empower patients to become actively involved in the management of their rehabilitation programmes; and the ability to instil instrumental rationality (the ability to select appropriate means to achieve a given end) in the patient.

props.name: goal setting
props.description: Collaborating with patient to identify and prioritize care goals, then developing a plan for achieving those goals.

props.name: pacing
props.description: Systematic progression of patient's activity level starting at a baseline level based on the proportion of tolerance followed by incremental increase.

props.name: informing patient
props.description: Provide patient with clear explanation of the findings.

props.name: advice
props.description: A professional opinion about what could or should be done about a medical problem.

props.name: giving feedback to patient
props.description: Providing feedback to patient on the outcome of the assessment and treatment progress.

props.name: patient education
props.description: Informing or instructing patients on the specifics of their disorder and/or its treatment.

props.name: patient referral
props.description: Sending a patient from one practitioner to another for health care services.

props.name: wound complication
props.description: A finding of development of a new problem at the site of an existing wound.

props.name: motor skills
props.description: Performance of complex motor acts.

props.name: bilateral
props.description: A positional quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's having two sides; two-sided.

props.name: unilateral
props.description: A spatial pattern inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's involvement of only one part or side.

props.name: biomedical discipline
props.description: A vocation, academic discipline, or field of study related to biomedicine.

props.name: anatomy
props.description: Conceptually broad array term referring both to the science of anatomy and the actual structure or morphology of an organism.

props.name: biomechanics
props.description: The study of the mechanics of a living body, especially of the forces exerted by muscles and gravity on the skeletal structure.

props.name: etiology
props.description: The cause or origin of disease.

props.name: direction
props.description: A physical quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's orientation in space.

props.name: position
props.description: A spatial quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's spatial location relative to other objects in the vicinity.

props.name: soft tissue
props.description: Refers to muscle, fat, fibrous tissue, blood vessels, or other supporting tissue of the body.

props.name: physiological mobilization
props.description: A passive oscillatory movement applied to a joint within the control of the patient. These are movements that can be performed actively by the patient.

props.name: accessory mobilization
props.description: A movement that cannot perform actively by a person, but can be carried out on them by an external force.

props.name: self mobilization
props.description: Self stretching techniques that specifically use joint traction or glides that direct the stretch force to the joint capsule.

props.name: complementary therapy
props.description: Therapeutic practices which are not currently considered an integral part of conventional allopathic medical practice.

props.name: acupuncture
props.description: The practice of piercing specific points on the body with very thin sterile needles in order to relieve pain or induce regional anesthesia.

props.name: acupressure
props.description: The application of non-invasive finger pressure along energy points throughout the body in order to relieve pain and induce a feeling of well-being.

props.name: gait training
props.description: Systematic activities that promote walking with or without assistive devices.

props.name: weight shifting exercise
props.description: Start position: Stand with equal body weight on both legs. Action: Shift the body weight onto the affected leg, hold and then return to the start position. Shift the body weight onto the unaffected leg, hold and then return to the start position.

props.name: agility exercise
props.description: An exercise designed to improve physical agility.

props.name: direction changing exercise
props.description: Start jogging forward, plant the foot of the injured leg and push off at a 45 or 90 degree angle. Repeat the sequence in the other direction.

props.name: figure eight running
props.description: Start position: Space two floor markers on the ground. Action: Run in figure of 8 patterns around the floor markers. Variations: changing speed, changing marker distance.

props.name: slalom jogging
props.description: Start position: Space floor markers on the ground and stand at one end. Action: jog forwards weaving in and out of the floor markers. Variations: changing speed; changing marker distance; dribbling or bouncing a ball.

props.name: slalom running
props.description: Start position: Space floor markers on the ground and stand at one end. Action: run forwards weaving in and out of the floor markers. Variations: changing speed; changing marker distance; dribbling or bouncing a ball.

props.name: speed changing training
props.description: Start jogging and then alternate between accelerating and decelerating whilst jogging.

props.name: acceleration exercises
props.description: Start jogging and then accelerate to a running pace then slow down to jog again. Repeat.

props.name: deceleration exercises
props.description: Start jogging and then decelerate to a slow jog. Repeat.

props.name: start and stop exercise
props.description: Run forward and then stop keeping balance on the injured leg. Repeat.

props.name: assisted exercise for range of motion
props.description: An exercise where a person performs a desired movement to the best of their ability with external assistance to complete a full range of motion and reduce resistance to the limb.

props.name: passive exercise for range of motion
props.description: Movement of a body part as a result of an externally applied force or a voluntary effort to move another part of the body.

props.name: exercise therapy
props.description: Therapeutic physical activities such as active/passive range of motion, isometrics, stretching, and weight lifting.

props.name: sport
props.description: Engaging in competitive and informal or formally organized games or athletic events, performed alone or in a group, such as bowling, gymnastics or soccer.

props.name: air sport
props.description: The term air sports covers a range of aerial activities such as: gliding, parachuting, paragliding, etc.

props.name: basketball
props.description: A competitive team sport played on a rectangular court having a raised basket at each end.

props.name: baseball
props.description: A team sport played with a bat and ball by 2 teams of 9 players.

props.name: cricket
props.description: Cricket is a bat-and-ball game played between two teams of 11 players on a field, at the centre of which is a rectangular 22-yard long pitch.

props.name: bowling
props.description: Bowling refers to a series of sports or leisure activities in which a player rolls or throws a bowling ball.

props.name: climbing
props.description: Moving the whole body upwards or downwards, over surfaces or objects, such as climbing steps, rocks, ladders or stairs, curbs or other objects.

props.name: martial arts
props.description: Activities in which participants learn self-defense mainly through the use of hand-to-hand combat.

props.name: dancing
props.description: Rhythmic and patterned body movements which are usually performed to music.

props.name: football
props.description: A game in which a round inflated ball is advanced by kicking or propelling with any part of the body except the hands or arms. The object of the game is to place the ball in opposite goals.

props.name: rugby
props.description: Rugby football is a style of football seen most prominently in two current sports, rugby league and rugby union. It is a full contact sport.

props.name: golf
props.description: A game whose object is to sink a ball into each of 9 or 18 successive holes on a golf course using as few strokes as possible.

props.name: gymnastics
props.description: Systematic physical exercise. This includes calisthenics, a system of light gymnastics for promoting strength and grace of carriage.

props.name: handball
props.description: Handball is a team sport in which two teams of seven players each (six outfield players and a goalkeeper on each team) pass a ball to throw it into the goal of the other team.

props.name: volleyball
props.description: A team sport in which two teams hit an inflated ball back and forth over a high net using their hands.

props.name: racquet sport
props.description: Any sport where players use racquets to hit a ball or other object.

props.name: badminton
props.description: Badminton is a racquet sport played by either two opposing players (singles) or two opposing pairs (doubles), who take positions on opposite halves of a rectangular court that is divided by a net. Players score points by striking a shuttlecock with their racquet so that it passes over the net and lands in their opponents' half of the court.

props.name: squash
props.description: Squash is a high-speed racquet sport played by two players (or in doubles 4 players on court at a time) in a four-walled court with a small, hollow rubber ball.

props.name: tennis
props.description: A game played by two or four players with rackets and an elastic ball on a level court divided by a low net.

props.name: weightlifting
props.description: Olympic weightlifting, also called weightlifting, is an athletic discipline in the modern Olympic programme in which participants attempt a maximum-weight single lift of a barbell loaded with weight plates.

props.name: track and field athletics
props.description: Sports performed on a track, field, or arena and including running events and other competitions, such as the pole vault, shot put, etc.

props.name: sprint
props.description: Sprints are short running events in track and field athletics.

props.name: middle distance running
props.description: Middle distance running events are track races longer than sprints, up to 3000 metres. The standard middle distances are the 800 metres, 1500 metres and mile run, although the 3000 metres may also be classified as a middle distance event.

props.name: standard long distance running
props.description: Standard long distance running events are races 5000 metres or 10000 metres long.

props.name: marathon
props.description: The marathon is a long-distance running event with an official distance of 42.195 kilometres.

props.name: long jump
props.description: The long jump is a track and field event in which athletes combine speed, strength, and agility in an attempt to leap as far as possible from a take off point.

props.name: triple jump
props.description: The triple jump, sometimes referred to as the hop, step and jump or the hop, skip and jump, is a track and field sport, similar to the long jump, but involving a 'hop, bound and jump': the competitor runs down the track and performs a hop, a bound and then a jump into the sand pit.

props.name: high jump
props.description: The high jump is a track and field athletics event in which competitors must jump over a horizontal bar placed at measured heights without the aid of certain devices.

props.name: pole vault
props.description: Pole vaulting is a track and field event in which a person uses a long, flexible pole (which today is usually made either of fiberglass or carbon fiber) as an aid to leap over a bar.

props.name: hurdling
props.description: Hurdling is a type of track and field race.

props.name: steeplechase
props.description: The steeplechase is an obstacle race in athletics.

props.name: shot put
props.description: The shot put is a track and field event involving throwing in a pushing motion a heavy spherical object as far as possible.

props.name: discus throw
props.description: The discus throw is an event in track and field athletics competition, in which an athlete throws a heavy disc in an attempt to mark a farther distance than his or her competitors.

props.name: javelin throw
props.description: The javelin throw is a track and field event involving throwing a spear approximately 2.5m in length. The javelin thrower gains momentum by running within a predetermined area.

props.name: hammer throw
props.description: The hammer throw is an athletic throwing event where the goal is to throw a heavy metal spherical object attached to a wire and handle.

props.name: skating
props.description: Using ice skates, roller skates, or skateboards in racing or other competition or for recreation.

props.name: skiing
props.description: A snow sport which uses skis to glide over the snow. It does not include water-skiing.

props.name: sport movement
props.description: A motion of the whole body or a portion of the body used in sport-like activities.

props.name: pivot
props.description: A movement in which a player with the ball steps once or more in any direction with the same foot while the other foot (pivot foot) is kept at its point of contact with the floor.

props.name: twist
props.description: The state of being twisted into a spiral; torsional stress or strain.

props.name: overstretch
props.description: To stretch one's body or muscles to the point of strain or injury.

props.name: overbend
props.description: To bend to excess.

props.name: sidestep cut
props.description: The sidestep cut is a maneuver in which the swing limb is placed laterally, away from the stance limb, toward the new plane of progression.

props.name: crossover cut
props.description: The crossover cut is a maneuver in which the swing limb crosses over the stance limb, toward the new plane of progression.

props.name: overuse injury
props.description: Damage inflicted on any part of the body due to overexertion of some part of the musculoskeletal system, often resulting from work-related physical activities.

props.name: age
props.description: A time quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of how long the bearer has existed.

props.name: wear and tear
props.description: Loss, damage, or depreciation resulting from ordinary use and exposure.

props.name: disposition
props.description: A quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's prevailing tendency, mood, or inclination.

props.name: accident
props.description: An unforeseen and unplanned event or circumstance frequently causing loss or injury.

props.name: blunt trauma
props.description: Injuries caused by impact with a blunt object where there is no penetration of the skin.

props.name: fall
props.description: Falls due to slipping or tripping which result in injury.

props.name: slip
props.description: The act or an instance of slipping or sliding.

props.name: trip
props.description: A maneuver causing someone to stumble or fall.

props.name: occupational accident
props.description: Unforeseen occurrences, especially injuries in the course of work-related activities.

props.name: N methyl D aspartate receptor antagonists
Neuroprotective therapy
props.description: Neuroprotective agents are used in an attempt to save ischemic neurons in the brain from irreversible injury.

props.name: Multimodal reperfusion therapy
props.description: The MMRT approach is particularly promising for patients with anterior circulation infarcts. MMRT, including mechanical thrombolysis, IA lytic drugs, clot retrievers and angioplasty with stenting, increases the chances of reperfusion in these patients.

props.name: Dietary factor
props.description: The consideration of dietary factors as a variable in disease incident, transmission, and control.

props.name: Intravenous thrombolysis
props.description: Intravenous (IV) thrombolysis with tissue plasminogen activator (tPA, alteplase) is the standard of care in the treatment of acute ischemic stroke in current clinical practice and the extension of the time window up to 4.5 hours after symptoms onset has been already approved by the European Medicines Agency (EMEA) and US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) agency and included in European and American guidelines recommendations.

props.name: Horizontal jerk nystagmus
props.description: Nystagmus consisting of horizontal to-and-fro eye movements, in which the movement in one direction is faster than in the other.

props.name: Dissociated nystagmus
props.description: Divergence nystagmus

props.name: Nystagmus-induced head nodding
props.description: Head movements associated with nystagmus, that may represent an attempt to compensate for the involuntary eye movements and to improve vision.

props.name: Vertical nystagmus
props.description: Vertical nystagmus may present with either up-beating or down-beating eye movements or both. When present in the straight-ahead position of gaze it is referred to as upbeat nystagmus or downbeat nystagmus.

props.name: Downbeat nystagmus
props.description: Downbeat nystagmus is a type of fixation nystagmus with the fast phase beating in a downward direction. It generally increases when looking to the side and down and when lying prone.

props.name: Gaze-evoked nystagmus
props.description: Nystagmus made apparent by looking to the right or to the left.

props.name: Vestibular nystagmus
props.description: Nystagmus due to disturbance of the vestibular system; eye movements are rhythmic, with slow and fast components.

props.name: Furosemide
props.description: Loop diuretics like furosemide may act by decreasing total body water and increasing blood osmolality, thereby removing water from the brain.

props.name: Gaze-evoked horizontal nystagmus
props.description: Horizontal nystagmus made apparent by looking to the right or to the left.

props.name: horizontal optokinetic nystagmus
props.description: Horizontal opticokinetic nystagmus

props.name: Endovascular Interventions
props.description: Several endovascular interventions are being evaluated for the treatment of intracranial or extracranial arterial occlusions leading to acute ischemic stroke. Options include emergency angioplasty and stenting, mechanical disruption of the clot, and extraction of the thrombus. In most cases, the mechanical intervention has been combined with either intravenous or intra-arterial thrombolytic therapy.

props.name: Congenital nystagmus
props.description: Nystagmus dating from or present at birth.

props.name: Spasmus nutans
props.description: The combination of pendular nystagmus, head nodding, and torticollis.

props.name: Congenital horizontal nystagmus
props.description: Horizontal nystagmus dating from or present at birth.

props.name: Mechanical Clot Extraction
props.description: Devices have been used to extract thrombi from occluded intracranial arteries.

props.name: Horizontal nystagmus
props.description: Nystagmus consisting of horizontal to-and-fro eye movements.

props.name: Rehabilitation nursing of hemiplegia
props.description: 对偏瘫患者采取心肺护理、大小便护理、皮肤护理、良肢位摆放、翻身方法等措施。预防偏瘫患者出现并发症和合并症。

props.name: pressure sore rehabilitation nursing
props.description: 护理工作者对卧床的患者采取定时翻身、骨凸起部位皮肤的减压及清洁，防治皮肤破溃的护理方法。

props.name: THAM
props.description: THAM is supposed to act by entering the cerebrospinal fluid compartment and neutralizing the acidosis-induced vasodilation, thereby reducing ICP. ICP-lowering properties as well as beneficial effects on edema formation and cerebral energy disturbance of THAM have been demonstrated in animal models of head injury. In animal models of focal cerebral ischemia, THAM infusion was associated with a significant reduction of infarct size, brain edema and lactate concentration.

props.name: finger skin temperature biofeedback therapy
props.description: 通过手指皮肤温度信号反馈进行治疗的方法。用于周围血液循环障碍、多发性神经炎等。

props.name: galvanic skin response biofeedback therapy
props.description: 通过皮肤电阻信号反馈进行治疗的方法。用于自主神经功能紊乱等。

props.name: Rotary nystagmus
props.description: A form of nystagmus in which the eyeball makes rotary motions around the axis.

props.name: Pendular nystagmus
props.description: Rhythmic, involuntary sinusoidal oscillations of one or both eyes. The waveform of pendular nystagmus may occur in any direction.

props.name: Horizontal pendular nystagmus
props.description: Nystagmus consisting of horizontal to-and-fro eye movements of equal velocity.

props.name: Monocular horizontal nystagmus
props.description: Monocular horizontal nystagmus

props.name: Seesaw nystagmus
props.description: Seesaw nystagmus is a type of pendular nystagmus where a half cycle consists of the elevation and intorsion of one eye, concurrently with the depression and extortion of the fellow eye. In the other half cycle, there is an inversion of the ocular movements.

props.name: Upbeat nystagmus
props.description: In primary position the Upbeat nystagmus beats upward. The associated oscillopsias are often very irritating, but the symptoms are usually transient.

props.name: intonation training
props.description: 改变患者说话时音调低或单一音调的训练方法。训练时要指出患者的音调问题，训练者可以发音由低到高，让患者模仿，也可以利用乐器让患者随音阶变化发声来克服音调单一问题。另外，也可以用可视言语训练仪器进行辅助训练。

props.name: Pulmonary embolism
props.description: Pulmonary embolism is an obstruction of a blood vessel in the lungs, usually due to a blood clot, which blocks a coronary artery.

props.name: Dyslipidemia
props.description: Abnormalities in the serum levels of LIPIDS, including overproduction or deficiency. Abnormal serum lipid profiles may include high total CHOLESTEROL, high TRIGLYCERIDES, low HIGH DENSITY LIPOPROTEIN CHOLESTEROL, and elevated LOW DENSITY LIPOPROTEIN CHOLESTEROL.

props.name: Orthostatic hypotension due to autonomic dysfunction
Low-to-normal blood pressure
props.description: Mild decrease of blood pressure

props.name: Orthostatic hypotension
props.description: A form of hypotension characterized by a sudden fall in blood pressure that occurs when a person assumes a standing position.

props.name: Congenital miosis
props.description: Abnormal (non-physiological) constriction of the pupil of congenital onset.

props.name: Moyamoya disease
props.description: MOYAMOYA, a Japanese word meaning "something hazy like a puff of cigarette smoke drifting in the air,''is the descriptive term we apply to a peculiar angiographic picture consisting of abnormal net-like vessels at the base of the brain. In addition to this abnormality, angiography usually reveals stenosis or occlusion of the internal carotid artery at the level of its terminal bifurcation together with abnormalities of the anterior and middle cerebral arteries. These changes are usually bilateral.

props.name: Single gene disorders associated with stroke
Deep venous thrombosis
props.description: Deep-vein thrombosis (DVT) is a common condition that can lead to complications such as postphlebitic syndrome, pulmonary embolism and death.

props.name: Coagulation disorder
props.description: Disorders involving the elements of blood coagulation, including platelets, coagulation factors and inhibitors, and the fibrinolytic system

props.name: Fish intake
props.description: Fish consumption may be inversely associated with ischemic stroke but not with hemorrhagic stroke because of the potential antipla-telet aggregation property of LCn3PUFAs.

props.name: Interleukin 23
props.description: IL-23 and IL-1β activate T cell-mediated innate immunity and promote secondary ischemic damage during the subacute phase of ischemic brain injury.

props.name: Low glycaemic index diet intake
props.description: Food with a high glycaemic index has been shown to increase the risk of mortality from stroke (ischaemic and haemorrhagic) in Japanese women and a higher dietary glycaemic load (GL) was associated with a greater risk of haemorrhagic stroke in Swedish middle-aged and older men, as well as an increased risk of total stroke, but not haemorrhagic stroke, in over-weight women.

props.name: Beta carotene intake
props.description: Beta-carotene, is the biologically active metabolite of vitamin A.

props.name: Excitotoxicity
props.description: The pathological process by which nerve cells are damaged and killed by excessive stimulation by neurotransmitters such as glutamate and similar substances. (Source: http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Excitotoxicity )

props.name: abciximab
props.description: Abciximab (ReoPro) is the Fab fragment of a chimeric human/mouse monoclonal antibody directed against the platelet glycoprotein IIb/IIIa (GP IIb/IIIa) receptor, the final mediator of aggregation. Abciximab appears to be safe when administered up to 24 hours after stroke onset, and it might improve functional outcome.

props.name: Stay away from alcoholic drinks
props.description: Moderate alcohol consumption

props.name: Gene expression
props.description: Transcient focal cerebral ischemia induces a complex change in genomic profile, including expression of new genes, upregulation and downregulation of genes, occurring distinctly in a temporal manner. Detection of gene changes after ischemia is just the first step towards understanding different molecular pathways and proteomics and peptidomics studies provides supplemental insights.

props.name: Glutathione
props.description: A tripeptide with many roles in cells. It conjugates to drugs to make them more soluble for excretion, is a cofactor for some enzymes, is involved in protein disulfide bond rearrangement and reduces peroxides.

props.name: Vitamin D intake
props.description: Higher intake of vitamin D (≥600 IU/d) was associated with a lower incidence of coronary heart disease and stroke, in men but not in women.

props.name: Reduced fat milk
props.description: Reduced-fat milk (vs full-strength milk) Consumption is associated with lower risk of stroke.

props.name: Apixaban
props.description:
Apixaban is a small molecule that acts as a selective inhibitor of factor Xa, which is a key coagulation factor located
at the junction of the extrinsic and intrinsic pathways of the coagulation cascade.

props.name: Congenital bilateral ptosis
props.description: Congenital bilateral ptosis

props.name: Primary prevention of atherosclerotic cerebrovascular disease
Unilateral ptosis
props.description: A `unilateral` (PATO:0000634) form of ptosis.

props.name: Triflusal
props.description: Triflusal is an antiplatelet agent structurally related to aspirin that exerts its antithrombotic effect by acting on different targets involved in platelet aggregation and vascular inflammatory processes. In addition, triflusal increases nitric oxide synthesis in neutrophils, resulting in increased vasodilatory potential.8 Triflusal has already shown its efficacy in several thrombotic diseases.

props.name: Progressive ptosis
props.description: A `progressive` (PATO:0001818) form of `ptosis` (HP:0000508).

props.name: Matrix metalloproteinases
props.description: MMPs are a family of 14 enzymes, a subset of which have been found to be active in brain tissue. The various MMPs function as stromelysines, gelatinases, colagenases, a membrane-type proteinase and a matrilysin.

props.name: Congenital ptosis
props.description: Congenital ptosis

props.name: High magnesium intake
props.description: Magnesium intake is, like potassium intake, inversely associated with the risk of stroke, ischaemic stroke in particular.

props.name: Congenital Horner syndrome
props.description: A type of `Horner syndrome` (HP:0002277) with congenital onset.

props.name: Bilateral ptosis
props.description: Bilateral ptosis

props.name: Warfarin
props.description: Warfarin, a coumarin derivative, produces an anticoagulant effect by interfering with the cyclic interconversion of vitamin K and its 2,3 epoxide (vitamin K epoxide). Vitamin K is a cofactor for the carboxylation of glutamate residues to γ-carboxyglutamates (Gla) on the N-terminal regions of vitamin K–dependent proteins .

props.name: Mechanisms of atherosclerotic cerebrovascular disease
props.description: Three basic mechanisms can result in cessation or diminution of f low to regions of brain: embolism from a proximal source with occlusion of the downstream artery; local occlusion, usually due to in situ thrombosis, of a proximal or distal artery; or global hypoperfusion.

props.name: Post stroke depression
props.description: Depression is a common complication post-stroke affecting approximately one-third of patients. The presence of post-stroke depression has been associated with decreases in functional recovery, social activity and cognition.

props.name: Limb shaking TIA
props.description: A transient ischemic attack which is typically associated with severe large artery disease with exhausted hemodynamic reserve is “limb shaking TIA”. It is characterized by 30–60 sec episodes of repetitive jerking movements of contralateral arm and/or leg and has been described with carotid occlusion but also with stenosis of intracranial vessels, e.g. middle cerebral artery or anterior cerebral artery. “Limb shaking TIA” is elicited in situations which dispose to low flow, e.g. orthostatic dysregulation, hyperventilation in Moyamoya disease, or by carotid compression.

props.name: Grain
props.description: Whole-grain intake was associated with a trend towards a reduction in the incidence of stroke.

props.name: Modification of a primary serum lipid biomarker
Tumor necrosis factor beta
props.description: A tumor necrosis factor family member that is released by activated LYMPHOCYTES. Soluble lymphotoxin is specific for TUMOR NECROSIS FACTOR RECEPTOR TYPE I; TUMOR NECROSIS FACTOR RECEPTOR TYPE II; and TUMOR NECROSIS FACTOR RECEPTOR SUPERFAMILY, MEMBER 14. Lymphotoxin-alpha can form a membrane-bound heterodimer with LYMPHOTOXIN-BETA that has specificity for the LYMPHOTOXIN BETA RECEPTOR.

props.name: Heparin
props.description: heparin has been used to treat thrombosis and stroke. Its anticoagulant action may retard the advance of cerebral thromboembolism while arterial recanalisation occurs and, by preventing deep venous thrombosis, it may decrease the incidence of pulmonary embolism - one of the causes of death following stroke.

props.name: Vascular disorder
props.description: Vascular disease is an abnormal condition of the blood vessels. Blood vessels (arteries and veins) are the tubes through which blood is pumped throughout the body.

props.name: Nitric oxide
props.description: Nitric oxide (NO) has one unpaired electron and can be regarded ass a free radical. NO generation and its reactive products with oxygen free radicals may be highly cytotoxxic.

props.name: Dietary Approaches to Stop Hypertension diet
props.description: The  Dietary  Approaches  to  Stop  Hypertension  (DASH) diet  contains  a  high  intake  of  plant  foods,  fruits  and vegetables,  ﬁ sh,  poultry,  whole  grains,  low-fat  dairy products, and nuts, while minimising intake of red meat, sodium, sweets, and sugar-sweetened beverages.

props.name: Binswanger disease
props.description: Binswanger’s disease (BD) is a type of subcortical vascular dementia caused by widespread, microscopic damage to cerebral white matter. The damage is usually the result of atherosclerosis (i.e., narrowing of arterial blood vessels) that reduces the supply of blood to subcortical areas of the brain, causing tissue to die.

props.name: Risk factor reduction
props.description: Risk-reduction measures in primary stroke prevention may include the use of antihypertensive medications; warfarin; platelet antiaggregants; 3-hydroxy-3-methylglutaryl coenzyme A (HMG-CoA) reductase inhibitors (statins); smoking cessation; dietary intervention; weight loss; and exercise. Modifiable risk factors include the following: Hypertension, Cigarette smoking, Diabetes, Dyslipidemiam, Atrial fibrillation, Sickle cell disease, Postmenopausal HRT, Depression, Diet and activity, Weight and body fat.

props.name: Ataxic hemiparesis
props.description: Ataxic hemiparesis is a well-recognized lacunar syndrome involving homolateral ataxia with accompanying corticospinal tract impairment.

props.name: Tecarfarin
props.description: Tecarfarin (ATI-5923) is a novel oral vitamin K antagonist. Unlike warfarin, it is metabolized by esterases, escaping metabolism by the cytochrome P450 system and thereby avoiding cytochrome P450-mediated drug-drug or drug-food interactions as well as genetic variations found in the cytochrome P450 system.

props.name: Inflammatory response
props.description: Ischemic injury triggers inflammatory cascades in the brain parenchyma that may further amplify tissue damage by many mechanisms. Within minutes of occlusion, there occurs upregulation of proinflammatory genes which produces mediators of inflammation such as platelet-activating factor, tumor necrosis factor α, and interleukin 1 β.

props.name: Contralateral thermoalgesic deficit
props.description: High sensibility to heat; pain caused by a slight degree of heat.

props.name: Paresthesia
props.description: Abnormal sensations such as tingling, pricking, or numbness of the skin with no apparent physical cause.

props.name: Apathy
props.description: Apathy is a frequent neuropsychiatric complication of stroke that, although often associated with depression and cognitive impairment, may occur independently of both. Its presence has been consistently associated with greater functional decline.

props.name: Vertical gaze paresis
props.description: Voluntary or reflex vertical gaze (tested by oculocephalic and caloric maneuvers and Bell phenomenon) is often abolished. One or both eyes may rest in a downward position. Isolated paralysis of upward or downward gaze occurs less frequently. In human patients with vertical gaze paralysis due to vascular disease, bilateral lesions are found in the midbrain tegmentum.

props.name: Foville syndrome
props.description:
Inferior medial pontine syndrome (or Foville syndrome) is one of the brainstem stroke syndromes occuring when there is infarction of the medial inferior aspect of the pons due to occlusion of the paramedian branches of the basilar artery. This infarction involves the following:
- corticospinal tract leads to contralateral hemiplegia/hemiparesis.
-corticobulbar tract leads to contralateral weakness of the lower half of the face.
-medial leminiscus leads to contralateral loss of proprioception and vibration.
-middle cerebellar peduncle leads to ipsilateral ataxia.
-abducent nerve roots leads to lateral gaze paralysis and diplopia.

props.name: Hemihypokinesia
props.description: Hemihypokinesia is  found in right hemispheric strokes as part of motor hemineglect, but can be found in basal ganglia strokes, including the thalamus, and catatonia in biparietal infarcts.

props.name: Large vessel atherosclerosis
props.description: Large vessel atherosclerotic disease, most commonly extracranial carotid stenosis, accounts for some 15–20% of cerebral ischemic events

props.name: Matrix metalloproteinase 1
props.description: A member of the metalloproteinase family of enzymes that is principally responsible for cleaving FIBRILLAR COLLAGEN. It can degrade interstitial collagens, types I, II and III.

props.name: Soda intake
props.description: Greater  consumption of sugar-sweetened  and low-calorie  sodas  was  associated  with  a  signiﬁcantly  higher  risk  of stroke.

props.name: Smoking cessation
props.description: Cigarette smoking is an independent risk factor for ischemic stroke, and growing evidence has shown that exposure to environmental smoke increases the risk of cardiovascular disease, including stroke. Smoking cessation is recommended in persons who have experienced a stroke or TIA.

props.name: Folic acid intake
props.description: There is a positive correlation between homocysteine levels and stroke. For this reason, guidelines on the primary prevention of stroke recommend the use of folic acid in patients with known elevated homocysteine levels.

props.name: Claude syndrome
props.description: Claude syndrome is one of the brainstem stroke syndromes in which there is infarction of the dorsomedial aspect of the midbrain secondary to occlusion of the small perforating branches of the posterior cerebral artery supplying this area. The infarction involves the medial aspect of red nucleus with the rubrodentate fibers, CN III nucleus and superior cerebellar peduncle. Clinical picture is characteristic and includes ipsilateral oculomotor nerve palsy and contralateral upper and lower limb ataxia.

props.name: Vitamin B intake
props.description: There is a positive correlation between homocysteine levels and stroke. For this reason, guidelines on the primary prevention of stroke recommend the use of B vitamins in patients with known elevated homocysteine levels.

props.name: Physical therapy
props.description: 又称"物理疗法"。应用力、电、光、声、磁、冷、热、水等方法对疾病进行预防、治疗和康复的方法。是物理医学与康复的一个重要组成部分。通常分运动疗法和物理因子疗法。

props.name: cerebrovascular spasm
props.description: Cerebral vasospasm may lead to permanent neurologic deficits of fatal cerebral edema. It appears to be mediated principally by the vascular musculature, but intrinsic neurogenic reflex activity may also play a part, as may control by an extrinsic innervation of the cerebral arteries.

props.name: Consciousness
props.description: The commonplace dictionary definitions of consciousness tend to fare better since they often state that consciousness is the ability to be aware of self and surroundings. These definitions are circular – given that awareness is often seen as a synonym of consciousness itself, or at least as a significant part of it – but in spite of the circularity, such definitions capture something essential: consciousness does allow us to know of our own existence and of the existence of objects and events, inside and outside our organism.

props.name: Posterior Choroidal artery infarction symptom
props.description: The PChA arising from the P2 segment of the PCA, and is subdivided into medial and lateral branches. They supply the pulvinar, part of the lateral and medial geniculate body, the posterior parts of the intralaminar nuclei, and lateral dorsal and lateral posterior nuclei. They also irrigate posterior portions of medial temporal structures, parts of midbrain and probably the subthalamic nucleus.

props.name: Chocolate
props.description: High consumption of chocolate is associated with a 29% (95% CI 2–48) lower risk of stroke.

props.name: anticoagulants
props.description: Anticoagulant therapy for acute stroke may only be considered after a brain imaging study has excluded hemorrhage and estimated the size of the infarct. Early anticoagulation should be avoided when potential contraindications to anticoagulation are present, such as a large infarction (based upon clinical syndrome or brain imaging findings), uncontrolled hypertension, or other bleeding conditions.

props.name: Hypervigilance
props.description: Hypervigilance may be caused by an increase in activity of systems maintaining wakefulness or by impairment of sleep promoting mechanisms as can occur with lesions of the anterior hypothalamus, thalamus or brainstem. Hypervigilance, insomnia, inversion of sleep–wake cycle and delirium often coexist in the same patient.

props.name: Visual field defect
props.description: Visual field defect

props.name: Wallenberg syndrome
props.description: The laterodorsal medullary stroke is the most common of those three syndromes and is named the Wallenberg syndrome, after Adolf Wallenberg (1862–1946), a German neurologist. Wallenberg syndrome and an infarct in the inferior cerebellum stroke can be seen in isolation or together, the latter being usually the case if the vertebral artery is occluded.

props.name: Transcortical motor aphasia
props.description: This is characterized by poor spontaneous speech but good repetition and comprehension. There is a variable naming deficit and the writing output is also poor. The localization of lesions is characteristically in the mesial frontal region or the supplementary speech area in the dominant hemisphere. These are often caused by an anterior cerebral artery stroke.

props.name: Lacunar stroke syndrome
props.description: Lacunar stroke syndrome (LACS) is a description of the clinical syndrome that results from a lacunar infarct.

props.name: Pontine infarct symptom
props.description: Pontine infarcts are one form of brainstem infarction involving the posterior circulation. Infarcts in the pons are typically focal in nature.

props.name: Vertebrobasilar dolichoectasia
props.description: Vertebrobasilar dolichoectasia (VBD) is an arteriopathy characterized by distinct dilatation, elongation and tortuosity of the basilar artery (BA) and the vertebral artery (VA). It is an uncommon vasculopathy of unclear aetiology affecting the arterial wall of vertebral and/or basilar arteries, which is easily misdiagnosed.

props.name: Vascular disorder due to drug abuse
Venous thromboembolism
props.description: Embolism of a vein by an embolus carried in a direction opposite to that of the normal blood current, after being diverted into a smaller vein.

props.name: Cathepsin B
props.description: is a mediators facilitate apoptotic cell death pathways.

props.name: Apoptosis
props.description: Apoptosis is an energy-consuming process, so reperfusion could potentiate apoptosis by restoring cellular energy.

props.name: Cerebral venous thrombosis
props.description: Cerebral venous thrombosis is an infrequent condition characterized by extreme variability in its clinical presentation and mode of onset.

props.name: Peripheral visual field constriction with 40-50 degrees central field preserved
props.description: Peripheral visual field constriction with 40-50 degrees central field preserved

props.name: Poly ADP ribose polymerase activation
props.description: PADP is a mediators facilitate apoptotic cell death pathways.

props.name: Large central visual field defect
props.description: Large central visual field defect

props.name: Inducible nitric oxide synthase
props.description: Inducible nitric oxide synthase (iNOS) is a key enzyme in the macrophage inflammatory response, which is the source of nitric oxide (NO) that is potently induced in response to proinflammatory stimuli.

props.name: Peripheral visual field constriction with 10-20 degrees central field preserved
props.description: Peripheral visual field constriction with 10-20 degrees central field preserved

props.name: Constricted visual fields
props.description: Constricted visual fields

props.name: Peripheral visual field constriction with 20-30 degrees central field preserved
props.description: Peripheral visual field constriction with 20-30 degrees central field preserved

props.name: Peripheral visual field constriction with 30-40 degrees central field preserved
props.description: Peripheral visual field constriction with 30-40 degrees central field preserved

props.name: Arcuate scotoma
props.description: Arcuate scotoma

props.name: Ring scotoma
props.description: Ring scotoma

props.name: Centrocaecal scotoma
props.description: A scotoma (area of diminished vision within the visual field) located between the central point of fixation and the blind spot with a roughly horizontal oval shape.

props.name: Peripheral visual field constriction with<10 degrees central field preserved
