props.description: Peripheral visual field constriction with <10 degrees central field preserved

props.name: Scotoma
props.description: Scotoma refers to an area or island of loss or impairment of visual acuity surrounded by a field of normal or relatively well-preserved vision.

props.name: Altitudinal visual field defect
props.description: Altitudinal visual field defect

props.name: Blind-spot enlargment
props.description: Blind-spot enlargment

props.name: Central scotoma
props.description: An area of depressed vision located at the point of fixation and that interferes with central vision.

props.name: Scintillating scotoma
props.description: A scintillating scotoma is a common visual aura that can preced a migraine, whereby a spot of flickering light near the center of the visual fields occurs. The spot prevents vision, and is thus termed scotoma. The scotoma can extend into one or more shimmering arcs of white or colored flashing lights.

props.name: Estrogen replacement therapy
props.description: The use of hormonal agents with estrogen-like activity in postmenopausal or other estrogen-deficient women to alleviate effects of hormone deficiency, such as vasomotor symptoms, DYSPAREUNIA, and progressive development of OSTEOPOROSIS. This may also include the use of progestational agents in combination therapy.

props.name: Ideomotor apraxia
props.description: Patients with ideomotor apraxia fail to execute purposeful, skilled or learned movements without this being due to elementary sensorimotor, extrapyramidal, or other cognitive disturbances. The disorder affects both the limbs contralateral and ipsilateral to a unilateral lesion which practically always involves the left hemisphere (in right handed subjects).

props.name: heavy drinking
props.description: Drinking an excessive amount of ALCOHOLIC BEVERAGES in a short period of time.

props.name: Lower extremity weakness
props.description: Weakness of the muscles of the legs. Inability to perform rapid, alternating movements.

props.name: Dysphagia
props.description: Difficulty in swallowing.

props.name: Conjugate gaze paresis
props.description: Conjugate-gaze palsy is one of the most common eyemovement abnormalities in patients with acute stroke. The eyes may be deviated to one side, either to the side of a hemispheral lesion or to the opposite side of a pons lesion, with gaze paresis towards the opposite side. This gaze palsy is almost invariably accompanied by hemiparesis.

props.name: Thermanalgesia of the limbs and trunk
Euphoria
props.description: An exaggerated state of psychological and physical well being.

props.name: Hemineglect
props.description: Hemispatial neglect is one element of the neglect syndrome. Neglect is operationally defined as the failure to report, respond or orient either to external sensory stimulation or mental representations of sensory events when the failure is not attributable to a primary sensory or motor deficit.

props.name: Risk factor
props.description: An aspect of personal behavior or lifestyle, environmental exposure, or inborn or inherited characteristic, which, on the basis of epidemiologic evidence, is known to be associated with a health-related condition considered important to prevent.

props.name: Ipsilateral facial paralysis
props.description: Facial paralysis can be caused by compression of the facial nerve.The main difference between facial paralysis and Palsy is cause for the paralysis can be identified, be it a tumor, infection, or nerve damage. Facial paralysis, in most cases, also appears more permanent than Bell's Palsy, with cases lasting for years to life if a patient doesn't seek treatment. Complete loss of ability to move facial muscles innervated by the facial nerve (i.e., the seventh cranial nerve).

props.name: Anarthria
props.description: Anarthria is due to bilateral facio-glosso-pharyngo-laryngeal paralysis, which also causes dysphagia and limits the use of facial expression in communication.

props.name: Anterograde amnesia
props.description: Anterograde amnesia is an inability to recall or recognize events, facts, or concepts to which one was exposed following the onset of illness.

props.name: Homonymous quadrantanopsia
props.description:
Homonymous quadrantanopsia is defined as the visual loss that is restricted to one quadrant of the visual field and is comparable in both eyes. Thus, when looking straight ahead, patients may have difficulty seeing objects or movement
in the upper or lower quadrant of the visual field, but it will be in the same quadrant (i.e., either to the right or to the left) regardless of which eye is being tested. Depending on the extent of the lesion, slightlymore or slightly less than one quarter of the visual field may actually be affected. Homonymous quadrantanopsia usually results from lesions posterior to the lateral geniculate nuclei, which encroach either on the optic radiations or the primary visual cortex.

props.name: Horizontal conjugate gaze palsy
props.description: Conjugate-gaze palsy is one of the most common eyemovement abnormalities in patients with acute stroke. The eyes may be deviated to one side, either to the side of a hemispheral lesion or to the opposite side of a pons lesion, with gaze paresis towards the opposite side.

props.name: Posterior cerebral artery infarction syndrome
props.description: The PCA is subdivided into four segments with associated clinical presentation. An occlusion of the proximal segment (P1 or precommunal) usually causes a total PCA infarction, including upper midbrain, variable parts of the thalamus and posterior hemispheric territory. Occlusions of the P2 (or postcommunal) segment before the branching of the thalamogeniculate arteries provoke ischemic lesions in the lateral thalamus and the hemispheric PCA territory. Lastly, cortical PCA branch occlusion causes diverse cortical lesions in the superficial PCA territory, including the occipital, postero-inferior temporal and variable part of the posterior parietal lobes.

props.name: Isolated monoparesis
props.description: Isolated monoparesis can be the clinical presentation in up to 4% of patients with lacunar infarcts.

props.name: paramedian artery infarction symptom
props.description: The paramedian arteries arise from the P1 segment of the PCA. The inferior and middle rami irrigate parts of the midbrain and the pons, while the superior ramus irrigates a variable extent of thalamus but mostly the dorsomedial nucleus, the intralaminar nuclei and internal medullary lamina. Infarctions also tend to involve the medial midbrain.

props.name: Upper quadrantanopsia without cognitive impairment
props.description: A rarer but typical presentation of AChA infarcts is the triad of contralateral severe hemiparesis, hemihypesthesia and upper quadrantanopsia or contralateral versus ipsilateral hemianopsia (in the case of lateral geniculate body or optic tract, respectively) without cognitive disturbances, in contrast with MCA infarction.

props.name: Headache
props.description: A headache is a pain or discomfort that is perceived to be in the head, although sometimes the pain may actually be referred from other structures such as the neck. Lifethreatening causes of headache, although rare, must be considered as more expedient treatment can be life saving.

props.name: Horizontal gaze paresis
props.description: Lateral gaze palsy is an inability to produce horizontal, conjugate eye movements in one or both directions. Lesions of the cranial nerve VI (abducens) nucleus in the pons cause ipsilateral, horizontal gaze palsy by disrupting motoneurons that innervate the ipsilateral lateral rectus muscle by way of cranial nerve VI, and interneurons that connect to the contralateral cranial nerve III nucleus in the midbrain, via the medial longitudinal fasciculus, to stimulate the medial rectus of the opposite eye. Lesions of the paramedian pontine reticular formation, adjacent to the abducens nucleus, may cause lateral gaze palsy, particularly involving ipsilateral saccadic eye movements. Lesions of the frontal or parietal cortical eye fields may also cause weakness of horizontal gaze (contralateral to frontal lesions and ipsilateral to parietal lesions) that becomes more subtle over time.

props.name: Complex hyperkinesias
props.description: The most complex hyperkinesia associated with stroke is found in association with posterio-lateral thalamic strokes, mostly posterior choroidal or thalamogeniculate. A mixture of rubral tremor, chorea, pseudoathetosis, myoclonus, dystonia and ataxia is regularly found, which has been called the ‘jerky dystonic unsteady hand syndrome’ by our group. When associated with a painful syndrome, this is well known as the Dejerine–Roussy syndrome. Very complex dyskinesia with dystonia, avoidance and withdrawal behaviors, hypertonia (poikilotonia), persistence of awkward postures (hemicatalepsy, levitation), akinesia, multiple apraxias, ataxia, and sensorimotor deficits is found in the parietal lobe motor syndrome, but also in temporo-parietal, basal ganglia and fronto-cingulate strokes (also see maniform agitation, compulsive motor behaviours and athymormic states above).

props.name: Anisocoria
props.description: Anisocoria, or unequal pupil size, may represent a benign physiologic variant or a manifestation of disease. Pathologic anisocoria can reflect an abnormality of the musculature of the iris or of the sympathetic or prasympathetic innervation of the iris.

props.name: Watershed infarction syndrome
props.description:
Watershed (or borderzone) infarcts represent about 5% of all strokes. They involve the junction of distal regions of two arterial systems. 
WS infarcts have been studied best in the anterior circulation in relationship to severe stenosis or occlusion of the ICA. Two typical patterns are observed: cortical WS (CWS) and the internal WS (IWS) strokes. The CWS area is located superficially in the cortex between the MCA, ACA and PCA territories. Strokes appear radiologically as wedges extending from the prefrontal or parieto-occipital cortex down to the frontal and occipital horns of the lateral ventricle respectively. The IWS area is situated in an anterior–posterior orientation in the centrum semiovale and along the lateral ventricle

props.name: Collier's sign
props.description: Collier's sign is well known as unilateral or bilateral eyelid retraction due to midbrain lesions. This sign is usually caused by infarction, tumor, multiple sclerosis, neuro-degenerative disease, or encephalitis.

props.name: Chorea
props.description: Chorea (Greek for 'dance') refers to widespread arrhythmic involuntary movements of a forcible, jerky and restless fashion.

props.name: Dyschromatopsia
props.description: A form of colorblindness in which only two of the three fundamental colors can be distinguished due to a lack of one of the retinal cone pigments.

props.name: Type I Hyperlipoproteinemia
props.description: An inherited condition due to a deficiency of either LIPOPROTEIN LIPASE or APOLIPOPROTEIN C-II (a lipase-activating protein). The lack of lipase activities results in inability to remove CHYLOMICRONS and TRIGLYCERIDES from the blood which has a creamy top layer after standing.

props.name: Complication
props.description: Medical complications of acute ischemic stroke are common and influence outcome after ischemic stroke.

props.name: push method
props.description: 增加软腭肌肌力的言语训练方法。将患者双手放在桌面上向下推；两手掌由下向上推；两手掌相对推或两手掌同时向下推同时发[au]的声音。

props.name: Delirium
props.description: Delirium is characterized by reduced ability to maintain attention; disturbance of immediate memory; and disorganized, slowed, and impoverished thinking. Disorientation, altered shortterm and long-term memory, illusions, and hallucinations are frequently but not invariably present. Although delirium usually is accompanied by decreased arousal and psychomotor slowing, occasionally it may be characterized by hypervigilance and enhanced psychomotor activity. Occasionally, there is a ‘dreamy’ or ‘twilight’ state associated with partial loss of contact with the outer world.

props.name: Amusia
props.description: Perception of music is impaired in most patients with auditory sound agnosia, but a disproportionate difficulty in recognizing melodies is referred to as sensory (or receptive) amusia.

props.name: Transcortical sensory aphasia
props.description: This is characterized by fluent, semantic jargon, poor comprehension and good repetition. These patients usually have far more posterior lesions, usually in the watershed area between the middle cerebral and posterior cerebral circulation, although at times thalamic lesions are described with ‘transcortical sensory’ features.

props.name: Ipsilateral tongue paralysis
props.description: Ipsilateral tongue paralysis is the least common but most topographically localizing sign of medial medullary infarction. Tongue weakness is probably most often related to involvement of the intraparenchymal XIIth nerve fibres as they pass ventrally to exit at the medullary base rather than to infarction of the hypoglossal nucleus in the tegmentum. Tongue paresis causes slurring of speech especially of lingual consonants

props.name: Impulsivity
props.description: Impulsivity is defined as a personality trait characterized by the inclination of an individual to initiate behavior without adequate forethought as to the consequences of his or her actions (impulse action), thus acting on the spur of the moment.

props.name: Tremor
props.description: An unintentional, oscillating to-and-fro muscle movement.

props.name: Optokinetic nystagmus
props.description: The optokinetic reflex is a combination of a saccade and smooth pursuit eye movements. It is seen when an individual follows a moving object with their eyes, which then moves out of the field of vision at which point their eye moves back to the position it was in when it first saw the object. The reflex develops at about 6 months of age.

props.name: Cheyne-Stokes respiration
props.description: This is well known in bihemispheric stroke, heart failure, somnolence, and brain edema with increased intracranial pressure.

props.name: Vascular parkinsonism
props.description:
Acute ischemic infarction of the caudate, putamen, globus pallidus, or brain stem can result in parkinsonism.
Parkinsonism of vascular origin is a controversial entity. Only 2% of patients with cerebral infarcts may have a parkinsonian syndrome.

props.name: Coca alkaloid
props.description: Coca alkaloids are the alkaloids found in the coca plant, Erythroxylum coca.

props.name: Episodic vomiting
props.description: Paroxysmal, recurrent episodes of vomiting.

props.name: Akathisia
props.description: Akathisia per se has not been reported in association with stroke, except in one case of unilateral akathisia in a posterior thalamic infarct. Cases of agitation or agitated confusional state have also been reported in association with various locations especially subthalamic infarcts but also caudate hemorrhagic and ischemic strokes, mesencephalic and substantia nigra, thalamic, right hemispheric or multiple lacunar strokes.

props.name: Hemihypesthesia
props.description: Diminished sensibility in one side of the body.

props.name: Tuberothalamic artery infarction symptom
props.description: The tuberothalamic (or polar) artery arises from the PCoA and irrigates the anterior nuclei, the ventral anterior nucleus, amygdalofugal pathway, mamillothalamic tract, rostral part of the ventrolateral nucleus, ventral pole of the medial dorsal nucleus and ventral part of the internal medullary lamina.

props.name: Ipsilateral third cranial nerve  palsy
props.description: Damage to the oculomotor nerve (III) can cause double vision (diplopia) and inability to coordinate the movements of both eyes (strabismus), also eyelid drooping (ptosis) and pupil dilation (mydriasis).

props.name: Calpain 1
props.description: Calpain 1 is a calcium-activated protease that has been specifically linked to glutamate receptors in the rat hippocampus. It is a mediators facilitate apoptotic cell death pathways.

props.name: Bell's palsy
props.description: Several conditions can cause a facial paralysis, e.g. brain tumor, stroke, and Lyme disease. However, if no specific cause can be identified, the condition is known as Bell's palsy. Named after Scottish anatomist Charles Bell, who first described it. Bell's palsy is the most common acute mononeuropathy (disease involving only one nerve) and is the most common cause of acute facial nerve paralysis. Facial nerve palsy is a dysfunction of cranial nerve VII (the facial nerve) that results in inability to control facial muscles on the affected side with weakness of the muscles of facial expression and eye closure. This can either be present in unilateral or bilateral form.

props.name: Contralateral fourth cranial nerve palsy
props.description: Paralysis of the fourth cranial (trochlear) nerve manifested as weakness of the superior oblique muscle which causes vertical diplopia that is maximal when the affected eye is adducted and directed inferiorly. The fourth cranial nerve crosses as it exits the midbrain dorsally and may be injured along its course through the intracranial space, cavernous sinus, superior orbital fissure, or orbit.

props.name: Dysarthria clumsy hand syndrome
props.description: Dysarthria–clumsy hand syndrome is due most of the time to a lacunar infarct in the basis pontis, less frequently to a lesion in the internal capsule or cerebral peduncle.

props.name: Forced grasping reflex
props.description: The grasp reflex is a flexion–adduction response in one or more digits, provoked by a distally moving pressure contact on a particular area of the palmar aspect of the hand.

props.name: High intracranial pressure
props.description: Intracranial pressure (ICP) is the pressure that is exerted on the brain, cerebrospinal fluid, and blood within the skull. In an adult at rest, it is usually less than 10–15mm of Mercury. If ICP rises above normal due to trauma, hydrocephalus, hemorrhage, or tumor, patients can exhibit behavioral changes, headache, decreased consciousness, somnolence, lethargy, seizures, and/or vomiting.

props.name: Graphomania
props.description: Graphomania, also known as scribomania, refers to an obsessive impulse to write.

props.name: Logorrhea
props.description: Logorrhea means excessive verbal production; it is manifested as an unusual verbosity that may suggest the presence of neurological or psychiatric pathologies.

props.name: Dysarthria
props.description: Dysarthria is a pure motor disorder of speech, occurring in 24–29% of patients with cerebral ischemia. It is characterized by dysfunction of the structures implicated in the control, initiation and coordination of speech output: lips, tongue, jaw, and palate, which are innervated by the facial, glossopharyngeal, vagal, and hypoglossal nerves.

props.name: Tetraparesis
props.description: Tetraplegia refers to a complete loss of strength, whereas Tetraparesis refers to an incomplete loss of strength. Weakness of all four limbs.

props.name: Nuclear factor kappa B
props.description: Nuclear factor-κB is a ubiquitous transcription factor that is a critical regulator of numerous responses including inflammation (Barnes, 1996) and pro-inflammatory genes such as TNF-α, IL-1β, nitric oxide synthase, HO-1 and intracellular adhesion molecule-1.

props.name: Behavioral disturbance
props.description: Infarction in the mesial frontal lobe can cause psychiatric symptoms, such as emotional lability, euphoria, paralogia, or witzelsucht. Restlessness, hyperactivity, anxiety, agitation, and talkativeness are also common among patients with unilateral caudate infarction. Patients with left-sided caudate lesions have shown a high frequency of severe depression. These behavioural and psychiatric disorders have suggested disturbances of frontocaudate circuits.

props.name: Vertebral artery infarction symptom
props.description: The vertebral arteries give origin to two arteries before joining to form the basilar artery: the anterior spinal artery, which supplies the medial medulla oblongata and the upper cervical cord, and the PICA, which supplies the inferior cerebellum and the dorsolateral medulla.

props.name: Alexia without agraphia syndrome
props.description: When the reading deficit occurs in the absence of other reading, writing or spelling deficits, it is referred to as ‘pure alexia’ or, as originally defined by Déjerine, ‘pure word blindness’.

props.name: Broca aphasia
props.description: This is defined as effortful speech output with hesitations, pauses, word-finding difficulty, phonemic errors (verbal apraxia) consisting of substitutions, deletions, transpositions and anticipations, occasional semantic errors, and agrammatism, but relatively preserved comprehension.

props.name: Projectile vomiting
props.description: Vomiting that ejects the gastric contents with great force.

props.name: Matrix metalloproteinase 3
props.description: An extracellular endopeptidase of vertebrate tissues similar to MATRIX METALLOPROTEINASE 1. It digests PROTEOGLYCAN; FIBRONECTIN; COLLAGEN types III, IV, V, and IX, and activates procollagenase. (Enzyme Nomenclature, 1992)

props.name: Dysphonia
props.description: An impairment in the ability to produce voice sounds.

props.name: Carotid siphon atherosclerosis
props.description: The carotic siphon (portion whithin the cavernous sinus) is vulnerable to atherosclerosis. Atherosclerosis within the carotid artery occures most frequently whithin the common carotid bifurcation and proximal internal carotid artery.

props.name: Lack of spontaneity
props.description: In language, verbal adynamia (lack of spontaneity of speech) is seen with lesions of the medial frontal lobes and refers to difficulty in initiation and maintenance of language output.

props.name: Wernicke`s aphasia
props.description:
This is characterized by fluent, paraphasic speech with impaired comprehension, repetition, and naming.
Neologistic jargon output is distinctive and occurs in severe Wernicke’s aphasia, associated with lesions of both the superior temporal and inferior parietal regions.

props.name: Tetraplegia
props.description: Paralysis of all four limbs, and trunk of the body below the level of an associated injury to the spinal cord. The etiology of quadriplegia is similar to that of paraplegia except that the lesion is in the cervical spinal cord rather than in the thoracic or lumbar segments of the spinal cord.

props.name: Anterior inferior cerebellar artery infarction symptom
props.description: The AICA vascularizes the dorsolateral inferior pons, the antero-inferior cerebellum, the cochlea, the labyrinth, and the VIIIth cranial nerve.

props.name: Vertebral artery dissection
props.description: Vertebral artery dissection is a dissection (a flap-like tear) of the inner lining of the vertebral artery, which is located in the neck and supplies blood to the brain.

props.name: Optic ataxia
props.description: Optic ataxia is a deficit of visually guided hand movements toward a normally perceived object in the peripheral visual field(s).

props.name: Hypercholesteremia
props.description: A condition with abnormally high levels of CHOLESTEROL in the blood. It is defined as a cholesterol value exceeding the 95th percentile for the population.

props.name: Hereditary hemorrhagic telangiectasia
props.description: An autosomal dominant disease characterized by the presence of multiple arteriovenous malformations that lack intervening capillaries and result in direct connections between arteries and veins.

props.name: Insulin resistance
props.description: Diminished effectiveness of INSULIN in lowering blood sugar levels: requiring the use of 200 units or more of insulin per day to prevent HYPERGLYCEMIA or KETOSIS.

props.name: Hyperlipoproteinemias
props.description: Conditions with abnormally elevated levels of LIPOPROTEINS in the blood. They may be inherited, acquired, primary, or secondary. Hyperlipoproteinemias are classified according to the pattern of lipoproteins on electrophoresis or ultracentrifugation.

props.name: Sodium intake
props.description: A higher sodium intake is associated with an increased risk of stroke; The  recommended  sodium  intake  is  <2.3 g/d  (100 mmol/d).

props.name: Type III Hyperlipoproteinemia
props.description: An autosomal recessively inherited disorder characterized by the accumulation of intermediate-density lipoprotein (IDL or broad-beta-lipoprotein). IDL has a CHOLESTEROL to TRIGLYCERIDES ratio greater than that of VERY-LOW-DENSITY LIPOPROTEINS. This disorder is due to mutation of APOLIPOPROTEINS E, a receptor-binding component of VLDL and CHYLOMICRONS, resulting in their reduced clearance and high plasma levels of both cholesterol and triglycerides.

props.name: Cavernous angioma
props.description: A cavernous angioma is a blood vessel abnormality characterized by large, adjacent capillaries with little or no intervening brain. The blood flow through these vessels is slow.

props.name: Hyperlipidaemia
props.description: Conditions with excess LIPIDS in the blood. Abnormally high level of lipids in blood.

props.name: Type V Hyperlipoproteinemia
props.description: A severe type of hyperlipidemia, sometimes familial, that is characterized by the elevation of both plasma CHYLOMICRONS and TRIGLYCERIDES contained in VERY-LOW-DENSITY LIPOPROTEINS. Type V hyperlipoproteinemia is often associated with DIABETES MELLITUS and is not caused by reduced LIPOPROTEIN LIPASE activity as in HYPERLIPOPROTEINEMIA TYPE I .

props.name: Capillary malformation arteriovenous malformation
props.description: This syndrome is characterised by the association of multiple capillary malformations (CM) with an arteriovenous malformation (AVM) and arteriovenous fistulas.

props.name: Fibromuscular dysplasia
props.description: Fibromuscular dysplasia (FMD) is a non-atherosclerotic, non-inflammatory disease of the blood vessels that causes abnormal growth within the wall of an artery. FMD has been found in nearly every arterial bed in the body. However, the most common arteries affected are the renal and carotid arteries.

props.name: Motor hemineglect
props.description: Motor hemineglect is characterized by an underutilization of one side of the body. It is a higher-order motor disorder that resembles hemiplegia although being substantially different from it due to a preserved motor output system.

props.name: Metabolic syndrome
props.description: The metabolic syndrome is associated with a higher risk of CVD, including stroke. According to criteria of the National Cholesterol Education Program Adult  Treatment  Panel  III  (ATP  III),  diagnosis  of metabolic syndrome is made when of the following risk factors are present:  abdominal obesity, elevated triglyceride levels, low levels of high-density lipoprotein  cholesterol  (HDL-C),  elevated  blood  pressure, and impaired glucose metabolism.

props.name: Subsequent herniation
props.description: Because the intracranial compartments are generally noncompressible and the intracranial volume is essentially constant, any additional pressure-producing solid or liquid mass within the intracranial cavity will result in displacement of healthy tissues. Supratentorial expanding mass lesions, such as tumors, abscesses, ischemic or hemorrhagic strokes, or traumatic hematomas, can produce herniation by displacing adjacent and remote brain tissue, especially diencephalon. Such displacement may occur across the midline (e.g., subfalcian herniation) or via the rostro-caudal direction by compressing the deep diencephalic and midbrain structures (e.g., uncal and central herniation).

props.name: Midbrain infarction symptom
props.description: The arterial blood supply to the midbrain is complex. Infarcts limited to the midbrain are uncommon and usually are accompanied by involvement of other structures such as the cerebellum, thalamus,andpons.

props.name: Diplopia
props.description: Diplopia is a condition in which a single object is perceived as two images, it is also known as double vision.

props.name: Facial paralysis
props.description: Facial paralysis can be caused by compression of the facial nerve.The main difference between facial paralysis and Palsy is cause for the paralysis can be identified, be it a tumor, infection, or nerve damage. Facial paralysis, in most cases, also appears more permanent than Bell's Palsy, with cases lasting for years to life if a patient doesn't seek treatment. Complete loss of ability to move facial muscles innervated by the facial nerve (i.e., the seventh cranial nerve).

props.name: Collagen type IV A1 associated vasculopathy
Balint syndrome
props.description:
The Balint syndrome is characterised by :
    simultanagnosia (inability to perceive more than one object at a time)
    optic ataxia
    oculomotor apraxia
It typically results from damage to the parieto-occipital regions, and has been associated with :
    corticobasal degeneration
    posterior cortical atrophy
    bilateral parietal ischaemic stroke

props.name: Active protein C resistance Leiden type
Metabolic disease
props.description: Generic term for diseases caused by an abnormal metabolic process. It can be congenital due to inherited enzyme abnormality (METABOLISM, INBORN ERRORS) or acquired due to disease of an endocrine organ or failure of a metabolically important organ such as the liver. (Stedman, 26th ed)

props.name: Type IV Hyperlipoproteinemia
props.description: A hypertriglyceridemia disorder, often with autosomal dominant inheritance. It is characterized by the persistent elevations of plasma TRIGLYCERIDES, endogenously synthesized and contained predominantly in VERY-LOW-DENSITY LIPOPROTEINS (pre-beta lipoproteins). In contrast, the plasma CHOLESTEROL and PHOSPHOLIPIDS usually remain within normal limits.

props.name: Auditory hallucinations
props.description: Phonism is a illusory perception appeared in the auditory illusory which is one of the common symptoms of mental patients, especially in schizophrenia.actually,there is no external acoustic stimulation to the auditory organ

props.name: Visual hallucinations
props.description: A kind of hallucination,which can see the image of a simple form. pathological illusion,if when awareness is clear which is more common in schizophrenia, while in the sense of disturbance occurs, which is more common in delirium or hazy state.

props.name: Focal dystonia
props.description: A type of `dystonia` (HP:0001332) that is localized to a specific part of the body.

props.name: Familial Combined Hyperlipidemias
props.description: A type of familial lipid metabolism disorder characterized by a variable pattern of elevated plasma CHOLESTEROL and/or TRIGLYCERIDES. Multiple genes on different chromosomes may be involved, such as the major late transcription factor (UPSTREAM STIMULATORY FACTORS) on CHROMOSOME 1.

props.name: American Speech & Hearing Association Functional Assesement of Communication Skills
Blepharospasm
props.description: A focal dystonia that affects the muscles of the eyelids and brow, associated with involuntary recurrent spasm of both eyelids.

props.name: Paroxysmal dystonia
props.description: A form of dystonia characterized by episodes of dystonia (often hemidystonia or generalized) lasting from minutes to hours. There are no dystonic symptoms between episodes.

props.name: Limb dystonia
props.description: A type of dystonia (abnormally increased muscular tone causing fixed abnormal postures) that affects muscles of the limbs.

props.name: Writer's cramp
props.description: A focal dystonia of the fingers, hand, and/or forearm that appears when the affected person attempts to do a task that requires fine motor movements such as writing or playing a musical instrument.

props.name: Craniofacial dystonia
props.description: A form of focal dystonia affecting the face, head or neck muscles.

props.name: Laryngeal dystonia
props.description: A form of focal dystonia that affects the vocal cords, associated with involuntary contractions of the vocal cords causing interruptions of speech and affecting the voice quality and often leading to patterned, repeated breaks in speech.

props.name: Retrocollis
props.description: A form of `torticollis` (HP:0000473) in which the head is drawn back, either due to a permanent contractures of neck extensor muscles, or to a spasmodic contracture.

props.name: Oculogyric crisis
props.description: An acute dystonic reaction with blepharospasm, periorbital twitches, and protracted fixed staring episodes. There may be a maximal upward deviation of the eyes in the sustained fashion. Oculogyric crisis can be triggered by a number of factors including neuroleptic medications.

props.name: Oromandibular dystonia
props.description: A kind of focal dystonia characterized by forceful contractions of the face, jaw, and/or tongue causing difficulty in opening and closing the mouth and often affecting chewing and speech.

props.name: Torticollis
props.description: Involuntary contractions of the `neck musculature` (FMA:71290) resulting in an abnormal posture of or abnormal movements of the head.

props.name: Paroxysmal choreoathetosis
props.description: Episodes of choreoathetosis that can occur following triggers such as quick voluntary movements.

props.name: Choreoathetosis
props.description: Involuntary movements characterized by both athetosis (inability to sustain muscles in a fixed position) and chorea (widespread jerky arrhythmic movements).

props.name: Evaluation table of clinical neurological deficit in stroke patients
augmentative and alternative communication system
props.description: 为言语或重度沟通障碍者设计交流策略和帮助系统的训练方法。常见的有文字、图片、符号交流板、便携式电子交流器等。可用于存在重度言语表达、阅读、书写、手势障碍者达到与对方进行沟通的目的。

props.name: Pulsatile tinnitus
props.description: Pulsatile tinnitus is generally classified a kind of objective tinnitus, meaning that it is not only audible to the patient but also to the examiner on auscultation of the auditory canal and/or of surrounding structures with use of an auscultation tube or stethoscope. Usually, pulsatile tinnitus is heard as a lower pitched thumping or booming, a rougher blowing sound which is coincidental with respiration, or as a clicking, higher pitched rhythmic sensation. Pulsatile tinnitus may be associated with vascular abnormalities such as arterioevenous shunts or glomus tumors or the jugular vein, arterial bruits related to a high-riding carotid artery (close to the auditory areas) or carotid stenosis, or venous abnormalities such as a dehiscent jugular bulb or to hypertension. Finally, in some patients, mechanical abnormalities such a spatulous eustachian tubes, palatomyoclonus (small spasms of muscles in the soft palate area), or idiopathic stapedial muscle spasm may represent the underlying cause of pulsatile tinnitus.

props.name: active exercise
props.description: 患者在无外力作用的情况下主动独立完成运动的训练方式。以增强肌力和耐力、改善关节功能、心肺功能和全身状况。可作为肌力3级患者的肌力训练。

props.name: Hyperglycemia
props.description: Hyperglycemia is common in patients with acute stroke, occurring in up to 60% of patients overall and approximately 12- 53% of acute stroke patients without a prior diagnosis of diabetes. Hyperglycaemia predicts higher mortality and morbidity after acute stroke independently of other adverse prognostic factors, such as older age, type and severity of stroke, and non-reversibility of the neurological deficit.

props.name: Endothelial dysfunction
props.description: In vascular diseases, endothelial dysfunction is a systemic pathological state of the endothelium (the inner lining of blood vessels) and can be broadly defined as an imbalance between vasodilating and vasoconstricting substances produced by (or acting on) the endothelium. Normal functions of endothelial cells include mediation of coagulation, platelet adhesion, immune function and control of volume and electrolyte content of the intravascular and extravascular spaces. Endothelial dysfunction is a risk factor for cerebrovascular events.

props.name: functional electrical stimulation therapy
props.description: 用低频脉冲电流按照预先设计的程序刺激已丧失功能的器官或肢体，以所产生的即时效应来代替或纠正器官或肢体功能进行日常活动的康复治疗。如：功能性行走、排尿、排便、吞咽等功能控制。

props.name: Dysesthesia
props.description: Abnormal sensations with no apparent physical cause that are painful or unpleasant.

props.name: Migraine with aura
props.description: A type of `migraine` (HP:0002076) in which there is an aura characterized by focal neurological phenomena that usually proceed, but may accompany or occur in the absence of, the headache. The symptoms of an aura may include fully reversible visual, sensory, and speech symptoms but not motor weakness. Visual symptoms may include flickering lights, spots and lines and/or loss of vision and/or unilateral sensory symptoms such as paresthesias or numbness. At least one of the symptoms of an aura develops gradually over 5 or more minutes and/or different symptoms occur in succession.

props.name: Migraine without aura
props.description: Repeated headache attacks lasting 4-72 h fulfilling at least two of the following criteria: 1) unilateral location, 2) pulsating quality, 3) moderate or severe pain intensity, and 4) aggravation by or causing avoidance of routine physical activity such as climbing stairs. Headache attacks are commonly accompanied by nausea, vomiting, photophobia, or phonophobia.

props.name: Thunderclap headache
props.description: Severe head pain with sudden onset, reaching its maximum intensity in less than one minute and lasting from one hour to ten days.

props.name: Migraine
props.description: Migraine is a chronic neurological disorder characterized by episodic attacks of headache and associated symptoms.

props.name: Cluster headache
props.description: A type of headache characterized by repeated attacks of unilateral pain lasting 15 to 180 minutes and associated with local autonomic signs.

props.name: Hypnic headache
props.description: A headache disorder that occurs exclusively at night, waking the affected individual from sleep.

props.name: Occipital neuralgia
props.description: A distinct type of headache characterized by piercing, throbbing, or electric-shock-like chronic pain in the upper neck, back of the head, and behind the ears, usually on one side.

props.name: Tension-type headache
props.description: A type of headache that last hours with continuous pain of mild or moderate intensity, bilateral location, a pressing/tightening (non-pulsating) quality and that is not aggravated by routine physical activity such as walking or climbing stairs.

props.name: Pain insensitivity
props.description: Inability to perceive painful stimuli.

props.name: Mediterranean diet
props.description: The  Mediterranean  diet  is  a  collection  of  eating  habits traditionally followed by people in the diﬀ erent countries bordering  the  Mediterranean  Sea.  This  diet  is  characterised  by  a  high  consumption  of  fruit,  vegetables, legumes,  and  complex  carbohydrates  (whole  grains);  a moderate consumption of ﬁ sh; consumption of olive oil as the main source of fats (monounsaturated); a low-to-moderate  amount  of  red  wine  during  meals;  and  low consumption of red meat, reﬁ ned grains, and sweets.

props.name: Coffee intake
props.description: the consumption of coffee (3–4 cups) has been associated with a reduction in the risk of stroke.

props.name: Comorbidity
props.description: The presence of co-existing or additional diseases with reference to an initial diagnosis or with reference to the index condition that is the subject of study. Comorbidity may affect the ability of affected individuals to function and also their survival; it may be used as a prognostic indicator for length of hospital stay, cost factors, and outcome or survival.

props.name: Treatment
props.description: Used with diseases for therapeutic interventions except drug therapy, diet therapy, radiotherapy, and surgery, for which specific subheadings exist. The concept is also used for articles and books dealing with multiple therapies. [MeSH] [LIRADS] Intervention with the intent to slow the growth, cause necrosis, or resect from the liver an HCC. Examples include surgical resection, ablation, chemoembolization, radiation, and systemic chemotherapy.

props.name: Fiber intake
props.description: ﬁbre intake has been shown to have an inverse association with the risk of both haemorrhagic and ischaemic stroke.

props.name: international classification of functioning, disability and health
Hufschmidt therapy
props.description: 应用低频电刺激痉挛肌和/或拮抗肌以缓解肌肉痉挛为主要目的的治疗方法。常用频率为0.66～1Hz，波宽为0.2～0.5ms的单路或双路方波电流，双路电流交替刺激时的刺激时间差常为0.1～1.5s。

props.name: High n-3 polyunsaturated fatty acid diet
tibial spine
props.description: A bony eminence in the intercondylar region of the tibia.

props.name: physical therapy
props.description: The use of exercises and physical activities to help condition muscles and restore strength and movement. For example, physical therapy can be used to restore arm and shoulder movement and build back strength after breast cancer surgery.

props.name: piriformis
props.description: A flat pyramidal muscle lying almost parallel to the posterior margin of the gluteus medius. It is partly within the pelvis and partly at the back of the hip joint. It is innervated by branches of the first and second sacral nerves and functions to rotate the thigh laterally and to abduct and to help extend it.

props.name: adductor longus
props.description: The most superficial of the three adductor muscles of the thigh and one of five medial femoral muscles. It functions to adduct and flex the thigh.

props.name: adductor magnus
props.description: The long, heavy triangular muscle of the medial aspect of the thigh. The adductor magnus acts to adduct the thigh. The proximal portion acts to rotate the thigh medially and flex it on the hip; the distal portion acts to extend the thigh and rotate it laterally.

props.name: adductor brevis
props.description: A somewhat triangular muscle in the thigh and one of the five medial femoral muscles. It acts to adduct and rotate the thigh laterally and to flex the leg.

props.name: sciatic nerve
props.description: The largest nerve of the body. Origin: sacral plexus (L4-S3), it leaves the pelvis through the greater sciatic foramen. Branches: divides into the tibial and common fibular nerves, usually in lower third of thigh. Modality: general sensory and motor.

props.name: tibial nerve
props.description: Origin: sciatic nerve in lower part of thigh. Branches: interosseous nerve of leg, medial cutaneous nerve of calf, sural nerve, and medial and lateral plantar nerves, and muscular and medial calcaneal branches. Distribution: while still incorporated in the sciatic nerve, it supplies the semimembranous and semitendinous muscles, long head of biceps, and great adductor muscle; it supplies the knee joint as it descends in the popliteal fossa and, continuing into the leg, supplies the muscles and skin of the calf and sole of the foot, and the toes. Modality: general sensory and motor.

props.name: common peroneal nerve
props.description: A terminal division of the sciatic nerve, passing through the lateral portion of the popliteal space to opposite the head of the fibula where it divides into the superficial and the deep peroneal nerves.

props.name: superior gluteal nerve
props.description: A nerve that arises from the fourth and fifth lumbar nerves and the first sacral nerve and supplies the gluteus medius and minimus muscles and tensor muscle of the broad fascia.

props.name: inferior gluteal nerve
props.description: A nerve that arises from the fifth lumbar nerve and the first and second sacral nerves and supplies the gluteus maximus muscle.

props.name: muscle of trunk
props.description: Muscle organ which is a part of the trunk. Examples: external intercostal muscle, external oblique, levator ani.

props.name: multifidus
props.description: A muscle with origin from the sacrum, the sacroiliac ligament, the lumbar vertebrae, the thoracic vertebrae, and the last four cervical vertebrae, with insertion into the spinous processes of all the vertebrae up to and including the axis, with nerve supply from the dorsal branches of the spinal nerve, and whose action rotates the vertebral column.

props.name: erector spinae
props.description: The superficial longitudinal muscle mass on either side of the vertebral column. It is sheathed in the fascia thoracolumbalis and arises in a broad, thick tendon from the sacrum, the ilium, and the lumbar vertebrae. It inserts into the ribs and into certain cervical vertebrae and is innervated by the branches of the dorsal primary divisions of the spinal nerves. It extends and flexes the vertebral column and the head, draws the ribs downward, and bends the trunk to the side.

props.name: transversus abdominis
props.description: One of a pair of transverse abdominal muscles that is the anterolateral muscle of the abdomen, lying immediately under the internal abdominal oblique. Arising from the inguinal ligament, the iliac crest, the thoracolumbar fascia, and the last six ribs, it inserts into the linea alba. It serves to constrict the abdomen and, by compressing the contents, to assist in urination, defecation, emesis, parturition, and forced expiration.

props.name: rectus abdominis
props.description: A muscle with origin from the pubis, with insertion into the xiphoid process and the fifth to seventh costal cartilages, and whose action flexes the vertebral column and draws the chest downward.

props.name: internal oblique
props.description: One of a pair of anterolateral muscles of the abdomen, lying under the external oblique muscle in the lateral and ventral part of the abdominal wall. It is smaller and thinner than the external oblique muscle. It functions to compress the abdominal contents and assists in micturition, defecation, emesis, parturition, and forced expiration. Both muscles acting together serve to flex the vertebral column, drawing the costal cartilages toward the pubis. One side acting alone bends the vertebral column laterally and rotates it, drawing the shoulder of the opposite side downward.

props.name: external oblique
props.description: One of a pair of muscles that are the largest and the most superficial of the five anterolateral muscles of the abdomen. It is a broad, thin four-sided muscle that acts to compress the contents of the abdomen and assists in micturition, defecation, emesis, parturition, and forced expiration. Both sides acting together serve to flex the vertebral column, drawing the pubis toward the xiphoid process. One side alone functions to bend the vertebral column laterally and to rotate it, drawing the shoulder of the same side forward.

props.name: trunk
props.description: Subdivision of body proper, which consists of a maximal set of diverse subclasses of organ and organ part spatially associated with the ribcage, thoracic and lumbar vertebral column, sacrum and coccyx, it is partially surrounded by skin of trunk. Examples: There is only one trunk.

props.name: step downs
props.description: Start position: Stand on the step. Action: Slowly bend the affected knee until the other foot lightly touches the floor in front. Keep the affected leg on the step and slowly straighten up the affected knee. Variations: adding hand weights.

props.name: jumping down steps
props.description: Start position: Stand upright on the step. Action: Jump off the step and land with equal weight on both legs. Variations: catching and throwing a ball; altering trunk position.

props.name: hopping down steps
props.description: Start position: Stand on the affected leg on the step. Action: Hop off the step and land keeping balance on the affected leg. Variations: catching and throwing a ball.

props.name: rotational hopping
props.description: Start position: Stand on the affected leg. Action: Bend the knee and hop to rotate around 45 degrees and land keeping balance on the affected leg. Hop in the other direction. Variations: catching and throwing a ball; on an uneven or unstable surface; adding upper body movements.

props.name: direction changing jogging
props.description: Start position: Stand upright. Action: Jog in a straight line, decelerate on the affected leg then push off at a 45 or 90 degree angle to continue jogging. Repeat the whole sequence in the other direction.

props.name: hamstring curl (standing)
props.description: Start position: Stand upright with the affected leg slightly behind. Action: Bend the affected knee by curling the heel upwards. Variations: adding weights around the ankle.

props.name: hamstring stretch (standing)
props.description: Start position: Stand and place your affected leg on a step. Action: Lean forward and feel a comfortable stretch down the back of the thigh/knee, hold and then relax.

props.name: high skipping
props.description: Start position: Stand upright. Action: Push off using the affected leg, bring the unaffected leg up towards your chest, land on both legs and repeat on the other leg. Variations: upper body movements; landing on one leg.

props.name: lateral step downs
props.description: Start position: Stand on the affected leg, sideways to the step. Action: Bend the affected knee so that the other foot lightly touches the ground. Variations: adding hand weights, upper body movements.

props.name: rotational lunges
props.description: Start position: Stand with the affected leg forward. Action: Slowly bend the affected knee and move the body weight forward onto the affected leg until the knee is flexed 90 degrees and directly above the toes while rotating the upper body to one side, then slowly straighten knees back to the start position. Repeat on the other side.

props.name: side steps
props.description: Start position: Stand upright. Action: Step out to one side and transfer the body weight onto that side with knees slightly bent. Return to the start position. Repeat on the other side. Variations: increasing the speed; on an uneven or unstable surface; throwing a ball at a target; adding upper body movements; adding hand weights.

props.name: sprint squats on step
props.description: Start position: Stand on the affected leg with the unaffected leg extended behind, resting on a step. Action: Slowly bend the affected knee as low as is comfortable and then straighten knees back to the start position.

props.name: forward stepping
props.description: Start position: Stand upright. Action: Step with the affected leg forward so the heel touches the ground, transfer the body weight onto this leg. Return to the start position.

props.name: backward stepping
props.description: Start position: Stand upright. Action: Step with the affected leg backwards so the toes touch the ground, transfer the body weight onto this leg. Return to the start position.

props.name: core stability exercise
props.description: A set of exercises to develop the strength and coordination of core muscles (including abdominal, lower back and pelvic muscles) in order to increase core stability.

props.name: single leg balance
props.description: Start position: Stand upright. Action: Lift the unaffected leg off the ground and maintain the balance on the affected leg without dropping the pelvis, using the arms or using the unaffected leg for support. Variations: tighten pelvic floor and lower abdominals; adding hand weights; on an uneven or unstable surface; throwing a ball at a target; adding upper body movements.

props.name: star excursion balance
props.description: Start position: Balance on the affected leg. Action: Reach with the unaffected leg forward as far as you can, maintaining balance on the affected leg and then return to the start position. Repeat in the other three directions, i.e. backward and out to both sides, maintaining balance on the affected leg throughout. Variations: throwing and catching a ball.

props.name: patella alta
props.description: A patella alta is an abnormally high lying patella.

props.name: patella baja
props.description: A patella baja is an abnormally low lying patella.

props.name: lateral shift of patella
props.description: An excessive shift of patella toward the outside (lateral) aspect of the knee joint.

props.name: lateral tilt of patella
props.description: An excessive tilt of patella toward the outside (lateral) aspect of the knee joint.

props.name: lateral subluxation of patella
props.description: An excessive subluxation of patella toward the outside (lateral) aspect of the knee joint.

props.name: dysplastic patella
props.description: An abnormal shape of the patella is, which may cause the patella to be unstable.

props.name: patellar hypertrophy
props.description: An abnormally small patella.

props.name: dysplastic trochlea
props.description: An abnormal shape of the trochlea, where the trochlea is flattened.

props.name: hypoplastic trochlea
props.description: Hypoplastic trochlea is a congenital abnormality where trochlea of the femur did not develop fully. It may lead to instability of the knee joint.

props.name: body mass index
props.description: A measurement to related body weight to height in an organisms typically calculated as the weight of an individual divided by the height of that individual squared.

props.name: body height
props.description: The vertical measurement of a body.

props.name: body weight
props.description: The heaviness or degree to which an entire organism's body is drawn to the earth by gravity.

props.name: self-management
props.description: Self-regulated modification and/or maintenance of behavior by self-governing of behavioral consequences. Used with disordered or normal populations of all ages.

props.name: prognosis
props.description: A hypothesis about the course of a disease.

props.name: diagnosis
props.description: The representation of a conclusion of a diagnostic process.

props.name: pathology
props.description: The medical science, and specialty practice, concerned with all aspects of disease, but with special reference to the essential nature, causes, and development of abnormal conditions, as well as the structural and functional changes that result from the disease processes. Informally used to mean the result of such an examination.

props.name: pain management
props.description: A form of therapy that employs a coordinated and interdisciplinary approach for easing the suffering and improving the quality of life of those experiencing pain.

props.name: rehabilitation therapy
props.description: In medicine, a process to restore mental and/or physical abilities lost to injury or disease, in order to function in a normal or near-normal way.

props.name: lifestyle therapy
props.description: Therapy dealing with lifestyle management and includes: behavioral and dietary modifications, exercise, stress management, and addiction control. This therapy must be used as major adjunct to 'standard care' or be applied as alternative treatment to conventional medicine practices.

props.name: professional role
props.description: The expected function of a member of a particular profession.

props.name: podiatrist
props.description: A doctor who specializes in the care of the foot and ankle.

props.name: pharmacist
props.description: A person trained in pharmacy that prepares and dispenses drugs prescribed by physicians and health practitioners. The responsibilities include instructing patients on the use, hazards, interactions, and side effects of any drug dispensed.

props.name: orthotist
props.description: An orthotist is a healthcare professional who specialises in the use of devices (orthoses) to support weakened joints, correct deformities and reduce pain and strain when the affected joints are being used in everyday life.

props.name: orthopedic surgeon
props.description: Orthopedic surgeons are healthcare professionals who use both surgical and nonsurgical means to treat musculoskeletal trauma, sports injuries, degenerative diseases, infections, tumors, and congenital disorders.

props.name: nutritionist
props.description: A professional trained and qualified to provide nutritional services at individual, institutional and community levels in term of assessing nutritional needs and coordinating them with medical ones, developing and implementing nutrition programs, evaluation and reporting their results, as well as to educate people on healthy eating, and diseases prevention and treatment by means of dietary modifications.

props.name: general practitioner
props.description: Physicians whose practice is not restricted to a specific field of medicine.

props.name: physical therapist
props.description: An individual trained and certified to apply knowledge of the concepts, principles, and practices of physical therapy for the treatment or prevention of physical disability or disease. Physical therapist plans and carries out treatment utilizing therapeutic exercise, massage, and physical agents such as air, water, electricity, sound, and radiant energy; performs tests and measurements involving manual or electrical means; and interpret results. Therapist also devises adaptations of equipment to meet the specific needs of patients.

props.name: personal trainer
props.description: A personal trainer is a fitness professional involved in exercise prescription and instruction.

props.name: nurse
props.description: A health professional trained to care for people who are ill or disabled.

props.name: injection of therapeutic agent
props.description: Administration using positive pressure and a needle or other equipment to drive a therapeutic agent into the body.

props.name: pharmacologic substance
props.description: A substance used in the treatment or prevention of pathologic disorders. This includes substances that occur naturally in the body and are administered therapeutically.

props.name: corticosteroid
props.description: A natural or synthetic analogue of the hormones secreted by the adrenal gland.

props.name: non-steroidal anti-inflammatory agent
props.description: A group of drugs that decrease fever, swelling, pain, and redness.

props.name: acetaminophen
props.description: A drug that reduces pain and fever (but not inflammation). It belongs to the family of drugs called analgesics.

props.name: hylan
props.description: Chemically modified sodium hyaluronate jelly used in reducing postsurgical tendon adhesions.

props.name: glucosamine
props.description: Amino sugar derivative of glucose, substituted at the 2 position, occurring in glycosaminoglycans and a variety of complex polysaccharides such as blood group substances.

props.name: cod liver oil
props.description: Oil obtained from fresh livers of the cod family, Gadidae. It is a source of VITAMIN A and VITAMIN D.

props.name: clinical history
props.description: A series of statements representing health-relevant qualities of a patient and of a patient's family.

props.name: pharmacotherapy
props.description: Treatment with any substance, other than food, that is used to prevent, diagnose, treat, or relieve symptoms of a disease or abnormal condition.

props.name: hip
props.description: The body part defined by the hip joint and surrounding structures, including the region from the iliac crest to the thigh.

props.name: long-term care
props.description: Care over an extended period, usually for a chronic condition or disability, requiring periodic, intermittent, or continuous care.

props.name: application of topical agent to skin
topical agent
props.description: A pharmaceutical preparation for topical application.

props.name: oral administration
props.description: The giving of drugs, chemicals, or other substances by mouth.

props.name: EQ-5D
props.description: EQ-5D is a standardised measure of health status developed by the EuroQol Group in order to provide a simple, generic measure of health for clinical and economic appraisal.

props.name: questionnaire
props.description: A document with a set of printed or written questions with a choice of answers, devised for the purposes of a survey or statistical study.

props.name: leg extension on all fours
props.description: Start position: Kneel down on all fours. Action: Find the neutral position of the spine by tilting the pelvis backwards and forwards and finding a position midway between. Tighten the pelvic floor and lower abdominal muscles, maintain this position and raise and extend the affected leg. Slowly return the affected leg to the start position whilst maintaining the neutral spinal position. Variations: adding arm movements.

props.name: bent knee fall out
props.description: Start position: Lie on back with knees bent and feet on the floor. Find the neutral position of your spine by tilting the pelvis backwards and forwards and settling into a position midway between the two. There will be a small gap beneath the lower back. Actions: Tighten pelvic floor and abdominal muscles whilst maintaining the neutral spine position throughout the exercise. Slowly let one knee roll out to the side, then return it back to the starting position. Repeat on the other side.

props.name: bridging
props.description: Start position: Lie down on the back with knees bent and feet on the floor. Action: Lift pelvis off the ground by pushing through feet, hold this position and then return to the start position. Variations: adding neutral spine position; extending the unaffected knee; placing feet on a step or a gym ball.

props.name: bridging on one leg
props.description: Start position: Lie down on back with affected knee bent and foot on the floor, the other leg extended out and off the ground. Action: Lift pelvis off the ground by pushing through the foot of the affected leg, then slowly return to the start position. Variations: adding neutral spine position; placing foot on a step or a gym ball.

props.name: clam
props.description: Start position: Lie down on the side with the affected side uppermost and knees bent to 90 degrees. Rotate the affected knee upwards as far as possible without moving pelvis. Return to the start position. Variations: lifting the uppermost leg so the feet are slightly apart.

props.name: leg lift
props.description: Start position: Lie down on the back with knees bent and feet on the floor. Find the neutral spine position by tilting the pelvis backwards and forwards and settling into a position midway between the two. There will be a small gap beneath the lower back. Action: Tighten pelvic floor and abdominal muscles whilst maintaining the neutral spine position throughout the exercise. Slowly extend the knee out straight and then return it back to the start position. Repeat on the other side.

props.name: dead lift
props.description: Start position: Stand upright with feet apart. Action: Squat down keeping the spine in a neutral position, pick up the weights from the floor, straighten the knees and hips to an upright position.

props.name: knee extension
props.description: Start position: Sit down with legs extended, the upper body slightly reclined and the ankle of the affected leg resting on a ball. Action: Push the affected knee towards the floor, tensing the front thigh muscles, hold and relax.

props.name: knee flexion
props.description: Start position: Sit upright with legs straight out in front. Action: Bend the affected knee as much as possible, hold and then slowly return to the start position. Variation: on a low friction surface that allows the foot to slide easily.

props.name: knee flexion overpressure
props.description: Start position: Lie down or sit upright with legs straight out in front. Action: Bend the affected knee as much as possible and apply pressure to the front of the affected leg to bend the knee more. This can be done using elastic resistance, a towel or hands.

props.name: skateboard slide
props.description: Start position: Sit upright in a chair with the foot of the affected leg on the skateboard. Action: Slowly extend the affected knee by sliding the skateboard forward, then slowly flex the knee as much as is comfortable by sliding the skateboard backwards. Repeat.

props.name: gastrocnemius stretch
props.description: Start position: Stand with the affected leg behind, knee straight, heel on the ground and foot pointing forward so that there is a comfortable stretch in the calf. Action: Hold this position.

props.name: gluteus stretch
props.description: Start position: Lie on back with knees bent. Action: Lift the affected leg, flexing at the hip and allowing the knee to rotate outwards. Rest the outer border of the ankle against the unaffected knee so that there is a comfortable stretch on the outer thigh. Variations: flexing the unaffected hip to increase the stretch.

props.name: hamstring curl (lying)
props.description: Start position: Lie on front. Action: Curl the heel of the affected leg upwards. Variations: adding weights around the ankle.

props.name: hamstring stretch (lying)
props.description: Start position: Lie on back. Action: Bend the affected knee towards the chest. Hold this position by placing both hands around the back of the thigh. Straighten the knee until a comfortable stretch is felt behind the knee or lower thigh.

props.name: heel raise
props.description: Start position: Stand upright. Action: Rise up on the toes then lower to the start position. Variations: standing with heels overhanging the end of a step; adding hand weights.

props.name: single-leg bent-knee heel raise
props.description: Start position: Stand upright and balance on the affected leg with the knee bent slightly. Support can be provided by holding on to a fixed surface. Action: Rise up on the toes keeping the knee bent then lower to the start position. Variations: standing with heels overhanging the end of a step; adding hand weights.

props.name: single-leg straight-knee heel raise
props.description: Start position: Stand upright and balance on the affected leg. Support can be provided by holding on to a fixed surface. Action: Rise up on the toes then lower to the start position. Variations: standing with heels overhanging the end of a step; adding hand weights.

props.name: inner range quadriceps exercise
props.description: Start position: Sit down with legs extended and the affected knee slightly bent with support underneath. Action: Push the back of knee against the support, tensing the front thigh muscles to straighten the knee.

props.name: resisted knee extension
props.description: Start position: Sit upright in a chair with the elastic resistance looped around both ankles. Action: Straighten the injured knee. Slowly return to the start position.

props.name: resisted knee flexion
props.description: Start position: Sit upright in a chair with the elastic resistance looped around the ankle of the injured leg. Assistance is required to hold the elastic resistance in front. The knee is extended in front. Action: Bend the injured knee against the resistance. Slowly return to the start position.

props.name: isometric hamstring exercise
props.description: Start position: Sit upright in a chair with the injured leg crossed in front of the other leg. Action: Push the injured leg against the other leg and do not allow the position of the injured leg to change.

props.name: prone knee extension
props.description: Start position: Lie down on front with the ankle of the affected leg resting on a ball. Action: Push the leg onto the ball to straighten the affected knee, hold and relax.

props.name: forward lunges with weights
props.description: Start position: Stand with the affected leg forward holding hand weights. Action: Slowly bend the affected knee and move the body weight forward onto the affected leg until the knee is flexed 90 degrees and directly above the toes, then slowly straighten knees back to the start position.

props.name: neutral spine control
props.description: Start position: Lie on back with knees bent and feet on the floor. Place hands on lower abdominals. Find the neutral spine position by tilting the pelvis backwards and forwards and settling into a position midway between the two. There will be a small gap beneath the lower back. Action: Tighten pelvic floor muscles and then the lower abdominal muscles. Spine and pelvis position should not change. Hold this position and then relax. Variations: sitting, standing.

props.name: single leg balance with weights
props.description: Start position: Stand upright holding hand weights. Action: Lift the unaffected leg off the ground and maintain the balance on the affected leg without dropping the pelvis, using the arms or using the unaffected leg for support.

props.name: prone extension
props.description: Start position: Lie down on front. Action: Raise the upper body off the ground, hold and then relax.

props.name: prone straight-knee hip extension
props.description: Start position: Lie down on front. Action: Lift the affected leg off the ground with a straight knee without allowing the pelvis to move. Variations: adding ankle weights or elastic resistance.

props.name: prone bent-knee hip extension
props.description: Start position: Lie down on front with the affected knee bent to a right angle. Action: Lift the affected leg off the ground without allowing the pelvis to move. Variations: adding ankle weights or elastic resistance.

props.name: quadriceps stretch (standing)
props.description: Start position: Stand upright and balance on the unaffected leg. Action: Hold the front of the foot of the affected leg and bend the knee. Feel a comfortable stretch along the front of the thigh.

props.name: quadriceps stretch (lying)
props.description: Start position: Lie on front. Action: Hold the front of the foot of the affected leg and bend the knee. Feel a comfortable stretch along the front of the thigh.

props.name: side plank
props.description: Start position: Lie on either side with knees bent and the upper body raised off the ground by resting on a flexed elbow and forearm. Action: Engage pelvic floor and lower abdominal muscles. Press through your supporting arm and straighten legs to lift your pelvis off the ground, to make a straight line between your shoulders, pelvis and legs.

props.name: knee extension (sitting)
props.description: Start position: Sit upright in a chair with feet on floor. Action: Lift the foot off the ground to straighten the affected knee. Slowly return to the start position.

props.name: soleus stretch (standing)
props.description: Start position: Stand in a step with the affected leg behind and equal body weight on both legs. Action: Keep the heels on the ground and feet pointing forward and slightly bend the knees so that there is a comfortable stretch in the lower calf of the affected leg. Hold this position.

props.name: sprint squats
props.description: Start position: Stand on the affected leg with the unaffected leg extended behind, resting on a supporting surface. Action: Slowly bend the affected knee as low as is comfortable and then straighten knees back to the start position. Variations: adding hand weights; varying the trunk angle; adding calf raises when rising from the squat; on an uneven or unstable surface; throwing a ball at a target; adding upper body movements; using a step to support the unaffected leg.

props.name: single leg balance with ball
props.description: Start position: Balance on the affected leg holding a ball. Action: Maintain balance on the affected leg whilst throwing and catching a ball.

props.name: squats with weights
props.description: Start position: Stand upright holding hand weights with feet shoulder width apart. Action: Slowly bend knees until the thighs are parallel to the floor, then slowly straighten knees back to the start position.

props.name: static quadriceps exercise
props.description: Start position: Sit down with legs extended and the upper body slightly reclined. Action: Push the back of the affected knee against the floor, tensing the front thigh muscles and hold. Relax and return to the start position.

props.name: sideway lunges with weights
props.description: Start position: Stand upright with feet shoulder width apart holding hand weights. Action: Step out to one side slowly bending the affected knee and moving the body weight forward onto the affected leg until the knee is flexed 90 degrees and directly above the toes, then slowly return to the start position. Repeat on the other side.

props.name: straight leg hip abduction
props.description: Start position: Lie on the side with the unaffected knee bent below and the affected leg straight. Action: Lift the affected leg upwards without moving the pelvis. Variations: tighten lower abdominals.

props.name: straight leg raise
props.description: Start position: Sit down with legs extended and the upper body slightly reclined. Action: Push the back of the affected knee against the floor, tensing the front thigh muscles and lift the straight leg about 20cm off the ground. Hold and then slowly lower the leg.

props.name: resisted hamstring curl
props.description: Start position: Stand with elastic resistance looped around the ankle of the affected leg and under the foot of the unaffected leg. Action: Lift the heel of the affected leg upwards to bend the knee without moving it forward. Variations: adding ankle weights.

props.name: resisted hip abduction/extension
props.description: Start position: Stand with elastic resistance looped around the ankles. Action: Move the affected leg away from the body and behind while maintaining an upright posture.

props.name: resisted hip abduction
props.description: Start position: Stand with elastic resistance looped around the ankles. Action: Move the affected leg sideways away from the body while maintaining an upright posture.

props.name: resisted hip extension
props.description: Start position: Stand with elastic resistance looped around the ankles. Action: Move the affected behind the body while maintaining an upright posture.

props.name: under leg lift
props.description: Start position: Lie on the side of the affected leg and the unaffected leg bent on top. Action: Lift the affected leg upwards without rotating the spine or pelvis. Variations: adding ankle weights.

props.name: steps
props.description: A set of aerobic exercises designed to improve the cardiovascular system, which consists of stepping on and off a special box of adjustable height.

props.name: hydrotherapy
props.description: External application of water for therapeutic purposes.

props.name: synovial membrane of articular capsule of synovial joint
superior tibiofibular joint
props.description: A joint between the lateral condyle of the tibia and the head of the fibula.

props.name: range of motion exercise for knee
props.description: Actions performed to provide the active or passive exercises to maintain knee function.

props.name: document
props.description: A collection of information content entities intended to be understood together as a whole.

props.name: data item
props.description: A data item is an information content entity that is intended to be a truthful statement about something (modulo, e.g., measurement precision or other systematic errors) and is constructed/acquired by a method which reliably tends to produce (approximately) truthful statements.

props.name: bone marrow
props.description: Soft, pulpy tissue; found in the marrow cavities of all bones and in the larger Haversian canal of lamellar bone; occurs in two forms, yellow and red marrow. In old age, undergoes degeneration, termed gelatinous marrow.

props.name: joint compartment
props.description: Anatomical compartment which has as its parts an articular capsule surrounding the joint cavity (or joint compartment space) and the content of that space which includes the synovial capsule.

props.name: anatomical entity
props.description: Organismal continuant entity which is enclosed by the bona fide boundary of an organism or is an attribute of its structural organization.

props.name: immaterial anatomical entity
props.description: Physical anatomical entity which is a three-dimensional space, surface, line or point associated with a material anatomical entity.

props.name: anatomical line
props.description: Anatomical boundary entity which has one spatial dimension.

props.name: subcutaneous adipose tissue
props.description: Adipose tissue located under the dermis. It binds underlying structures with the skin. The subcutis is important in the regulation of temperature of the skin itself and the body. The size of this layer varies throughout the body and from subject to subject.

props.name: Osgood-Schlatter disease
props.description: Osgood-Schlatter disease is a traction apophysitis of the anterior tibial tubercle described in active adolescents and characterized by gradual onset of pain and swelling of the anterior knee causing limping that usually disappears at the end of growth.

props.name: transverse fracture
props.description: A fracture in which the line of break forms a right angle with the axis of the bone.

props.name: angulated fracture
props.description: A fracture in which the fragments of bone are at angles to one another.

props.name: avulsion fracture
props.description: Separation of a small fragment of bone cortex at the site of attachment of a ligament or tendon.

props.name: butterfly fracture
props.description: A bone break in which the center fragment contained by two cracks forms a triangle.

props.name: comminuted fracture
props.description: A fracture in which the bone is splintered or crushed.

props.name: displaced fracture
props.description: A traumatic bone break in which two ends of a fractured bone are separated and out of their normal positions.

props.name: undisplaced fracture
props.description: A bone break in which cracks in the bone may radiate in several directions but the bone fragments do not separate.

props.name: epiphyseal fracture
props.description: A fracture involving the epiphyseal plate of a long bone, which causes separation or fragmentation of the plate.

props.name: extra-articular fracture
props.description: A fracture that does not involve a joint space.

props.name: intra-articular fracture
props.description: A fracture that involves a joint space.

props.name: incomplete fracture
props.description: A fracture which does not entirely destroy the continuity of the bone.

props.name: linear fracture
props.description: A fracture that runs parallel to the long axis of a bone.

props.name: oblique fracture
props.description: A fracture in which the line of break runs obliquely to the axis of the bone.

props.name: osteochondral fracture
props.description: A fracture involving the articular cartilage and underlying bone.

props.name: subchondral fracture
props.description: A fracture below the articular cartilage.

props.name: chondral fracture
props.description: A fracture involving the articular cartilage.

props.name: pathological fracture
props.description: A fracture occurring as a result of disease of a bone or from some undiscoverable cause and not due to trauma.

props.name: spiral fracture
props.description: A fracture of a long bone characterised by a spiral fracture line resulting from a torsional traumatic force.

props.name: stellate fracture
props.description: A fracture in which there are numerous fissures radiating from the central point of impact or injury throughout surrounding bone tissue.

props.name: stress fracture
props.description: A fracture due to the strain caused by repetitive exercise.

props.name: insufficiency fracture
